Descent.Blindness.forbiddenOverlap_of_le: q ∈ LevelResolvedForbiddenCore active weight energy overlap target
Descent.Blindness.forbiddenInterval_of_l: Set.Ioo lower upper ⊆ LevelResolvedForbiddenCore active weight energy overlap target
Descent.Conditionals.pooledCohort_forbid: ∀ leftLevel rightLevel, Blindness.AdmissibleLevels active weight target leftLevel → Blindness.AdmissibleLevels active weight target rightLevel → ∃ cohort ∈ active, q ∉ Blindness.ComponentAchievableOverlaps fitness overlap leftLevel rightLevel cohort

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.LevelResolvedAchievableEnvelope
definitions.signature: (active : Finset Index) (weight : Index → R) (energy : Index → Config → R) (overlap : Config → Config → Overlap) (target : R) : Set Overlap
definitions.body:
{q | ∃ leftLevel rightLevel : Index → R,
    AdmissibleLevels active weight target leftLevel ∧
      AdmissibleLevels active weight target rightLevel ∧
        ∀ k ∈ active,
          q ∈ ComponentAchievableOverlaps energy overlap leftLevel rightLevel k}
definitions.docstring: The level-resolved outer approximation to the superposed achievable-overlap set.

hypotheses: q ∈ SuperposedAchievableOverlaps active weight energy overlap target

Descent.Blindness.superposedAchievableOv: q ∈ SuperposedAchievableOverlaps active weight energy overlap target

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.LevelResolvedForbiddenCore
definitions.signature: (active : Finset Index) (weight : Index → R) (energy : Index → Config → R) (overlap : Config → Config → Overlap) (target : R) : Set Overlap
definitions.body:
{q | ∀ leftLevel rightLevel : Index → R,
    AdmissibleLevels active weight target leftLevel →
      AdmissibleLevels active weight target rightLevel →
        ∃ k ∈ active,
          q ∉ ComponentAchievableOverlaps energy overlap leftLevel rightLevel k}
definitions.docstring:
The dual level-resolved forbidden core: every admissible pair of level vectors is blocked
by at least one active component.

hypotheses: q ∈ LevelResolvedForbiddenCore active weight energy overlap target
Set.Ioo lower upper ⊆ LevelResolvedForbiddenCore active weight energy overlap target

Descent.Blindness.forbiddenOverlap_of_le: q ∈ LevelResolvedForbiddenCore active weight energy overlap target
Descent.Blindness.forbiddenInterval_of_l: Set.Ioo lower upper ⊆ LevelResolvedForbiddenCore active weight energy overlap target

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.oneHotWeight
definitions.docstring: A simplex vertex selecting one component landscape.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.translatedForbiddenBand
definitions.signature: (start velocity width mix : ℝ) : Set ℝ
definitions.body: Set.Ioo (start + velocity * mix) (start + velocity * mix + width)
definitions.docstring: An open forbidden band with fixed width whose left endpoint moves affinely in `mix`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.migratingForbiddenBand
definitions.docstring:
The concrete unit-width band used to refute the endpoint-disjointness heuristic.

    Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM. This is a counterexample, chosen
    for its arithmetic and not offered as a description of any migrating
    population. Its job is to show that a heuristic fails, which one instance
    suffices to do -- and a measurement finding no real population shaped like
    this would leave the refutation untouched, which is what makes it a
    counterexample rather than a claim.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.mixedSphericalCovariance
definitions.docstring: Even mixed spherical covariance with a shared quadratic component and two tail terms.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.sphericalGaplessnessCertificate
definitions.docstring:
The polynomial certificate `2 ξ'' ξ'''' - 3 (ξ''')²` for
`ξ(q) = q² + alpha q⁴ + beta q⁶`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.goldenCorrelationThreshold
definitions.docstring:
The positive root of `r² + r - 1 = 0`.  It is the correlation threshold at which the
two-block population overlap profile changes from monotone to gapped.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.populationOverlapProfile
definitions.docstring:
Population overlap profile for the rank-two correlated sparse-design witness.  Here `x`
is the missed-support fraction and `q` is the squared active correlation.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.populationGapCertificate
definitions.docstring:
Endpoint derivative numerator of the overlap profile.  Its sign detects whether the
profile turns down before reaching the disjoint-support endpoint.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.pooledEnvironmentCorrelations
definitions.signature: {Environment : Type*} (active : Finset Environment) (mass correlation : Environment → ℝ) : ℝ
definitions.body: ∑ environment ∈ active, mass environment * correlation environment
definitions.docstring: Effective active correlation of a finite collection of environments.

hypotheses: ∀ environment ∈ active, correlation environment ∈ Set.Icc lower upper

Descent.Blindness.pooledEnvironmentCorre: ∀ environment ∈ active, correlation environment ∈ Set.Icc lower upper

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.pooledEnvironmentCorrelation
definitions.docstring: Effective active correlation obtained by pooling arbitrary left and right environments.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.mixedEnvironmentCorrelation
definitions.docstring:
Effective active correlation when the `+rho` environment has mass `mix` and the `-rho`
environment has mass `1 - mix`.

    Empirical status: VALIDATED. Battery `gap01` draws 1e5 pairs per block, 20 blocks
    per cell, from two environments with correlations `+rho` and `-rho` pooled at mass
    `mix`, and measures the realised Pearson correlation of the pooled sample. This body
    matches at 2.06 sems.

Power: the check separates this equation from the reading that counts only the positive
environment. `rho * mix` is the natural mistake here -- it is what "mass `mix` of the
`+rho` environment" sounds like -- and the battery rejects it at 473 sems, with the
positive control (pooled marginal variance, known to be 1) passing at 1.55. The margin
is the sign cancellation: at `mix = 1/2` this body is 0 and the rival is `rho/2`, so the
two cannot both survive a balanced mixture. See `mixedEnvironmentCorrelation_half`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.criticalMinorityProportion
definitions.docstring: Critical minority-environment fraction for a positive pure-environment correlation.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.configurationOverlap
definitions.docstring: Euclidean overlap, the coordinate used by the classical isotropic band calculation.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.covarianceDisplacementEnergy
definitions.docstring: Energy scale of the displacement from a planted configuration under covariance `sigma`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.symmetricTwoCoordinateCovariance
definitions.docstring: General symmetric two-coordinate covariance.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.overlapEnergyWitnessCovariance
definitions.docstring: A positive anisotropic covariance with eigen-directions rotated relative to coordinates.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.demeRate
definitions.body: if i = j then 0 else if i = 0 ∨ j = 0 then a else b
definitions.docstring:
Symmetric gene-flow rates on three demes: `a` between the hub `0` and each leaf, and `b`
directly between the two leaves.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.generatorApply
definitions.signature: (q : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℝ) (f : Fin 3 → ℝ) (i : Fin 3) : ℝ
definitions.body: ∑ j, q i j * (f j - f i)
definitions.docstring: Action of a rate matrix on a function of the state.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.Lumped
definitions.docstring: A function of the state that cannot separate the two covariance-indistinguishable demes.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.generatorIter
definitions.signature: (q : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℝ) (f : Fin 3 → ℝ) : ℕ → (Fin 3 → ℝ)
definitions.body:
| 0 => f
  | n + 1 => generatorApply q (generatorIter q f n)
definitions.docstring: Iterated action of the generator: the observable process at every order.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.SuccessfulFamilyMark
definitions.docstring: A successful family is marked by eventual population fraction and front displacement.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.familyFraction
definitions.docstring: Eventual fraction of the population descended from a successful family.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.frontDisplacement
definitions.docstring: Displacement of the front caused by a successful family.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.genealogyMeasure
definitions.body:
Measure.map familyFraction
    (ν.withDensity fun mark ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (familyFraction mark ^ 2))
definitions.docstring:
The unconditioned genealogy measure induced by a marked successful-family intensity.

This is the literal measure-theoretic formula `Λ₀(dx) = x² ν(dx, ℝ)`: weight the marked measure
by `x²`, then push it forward along the family-fraction coordinate.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.HasFiniteGenealogicalIntensity
definitions.docstring:
The finite-second-moment hypothesis on the marked successful-family intensity.  It is exactly
the condition ensuring that the induced genealogy measure has finite total mass.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.speedTiltWeight
definitions.docstring: Exponential weight applied to a marked breakout by a canonical front-speed tilt.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.speedTiltedGenealogyMeasure
definitions.body:
Measure.map familyFraction
    (ν.withDensity fun mark ↦
      ENNReal.ofReal (familyFraction mark ^ 2 * speedTiltWeight theta mark))
definitions.docstring:
The complete conditioned genealogy formula
`Λθ(dx) = x² ∫ exp(-θr) ν(dx,dr)` as an actual measure.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.markedEventMergerRate
definitions.body:
∫⁻ mark, ENNReal.ofReal
    (familyFraction mark ^ k * (1 - familyFraction mark) ^ (b - k)) ∂ν
definitions.docstring:
Rate functional obtained directly from Bernoulli participation in marked events.  It is
`ℝ≥0∞`-valued so the definition remains meaningful before imposing the finite-second-moment
assumption used for a finite-rate coalescent.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.markedLambdaMergerRate
definitions.body:
∫⁻ mark, ENNReal.ofReal
    (familyFraction mark ^ 2 *
      (familyFraction mark ^ (k - 2) * (1 - familyFraction mark) ^ (b - k))) ∂ν
definitions.docstring: The same rate written in `Λ`-coalescent form with the `x²` genealogical weight exposed.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.logDisplacement
definitions.docstring:
Front displacement caused by a family that reaches fraction `x`, in the form that produces
the Beta family: logarithmic in the surviving fraction, with rate constant `γ`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.HasBetaTiltInvariant
definitions.body:
∀ x theta, x < 1 →
    conditionalLaplace x theta =
      conditionalLaplace 0 theta * (1 - x) ^ (theta / gamma)
definitions.docstring:
Conditional Laplace transforms have the Beta invariant when centering by the logarithmic
response leaves a transform independent of the family fraction.  If Laplace transforms determine
the conditional laws, this is precisely the distributional representation
`R | X=x = -γ⁻¹ log(1-x) + Z` with the law of `Z` independent of `x`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.HasFractionIndependentCenteredTransform
definitions.body:
∀ x y theta, x < 1 → y < 1 →
    conditionalLaplace x theta / (1 - x) ^ (theta / gamma) =
      conditionalLaplace y theta / (1 - y) ^ (theta / gamma)
definitions.docstring:
Centering a conditional displacement transform by the logarithmic response leaves the same
Laplace transform at every family fraction.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.linearDisplacementTripleRate
definitions.docstring:
Normalized three-lineage merger rate for the same unconditioned uniform `Λ₀`, but with linear
response `r(x)=x`.  This is
`∫₀¹ x exp(-θx) dx / ∫₀¹ exp(-θx) dx` in closed form.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.pioneerFraction
definitions.docstring:
Population fraction eventually reached by a pioneer of `advantage = B exp(γδ)`, after
relaxation against a front of width `width` with susceptibility exponent `p`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.MarkedBreakout.genealogicalTimescale
definitions.docstring: Genealogical timescale produced by the pioneer substitution.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.speedTiltFullMergerRate
definitions.docstring:
Full-merger moment for `extra + 2` lineages under the normalized
`Beta(1, β + 1)` merger law.  The product form is the integer identity

`(β + 1) B(extra + 1, β + 1)
  = ∏ j < extra, (j + 1) / (β + j + 2)`.

Using `extra` rather than a merger size makes the total definition free of truncated
subtraction.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.speedTiltNonMergerFactor
definitions.body:
∏ j ∈ Finset.range extra,
    (β + (j : ℝ) + 1) / (β + (k : ℝ) + (j : ℝ))
definitions.docstring:
Multiplicative penalty contributed by `extra` lineages outside a specified merging
`k`-tuple.  This is the finite Gamma-ratio identity

`Gamma(β + extra + 1) / Gamma(β + 1) * Gamma(β + k) / Gamma(β + k + extra)`.

The product form stays elementary and makes positivity transparent on `β > -1`, `2 ≤ k`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.speedTiltBetaMergerRate
definitions.body: speedTiltFullMergerRate β (k - 2) * speedTiltNonMergerFactor β k (b - k)
definitions.docstring:
All `b`-lineage, specified-`k`-tuple rates under the normalized
`Beta(1, β + 1)` law.  This is the exact finite-product form of

`(β + 1) * B(k - 1, β + b - k + 1)`.

The first factor is the full `k`-merger moment; the second is the penalty that each of the
`b-k` outside lineages avoids the merging parent.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.speedTiltCollisionScaleCoefficient
definitions.docstring:
Pair-collision coefficient relative to the tail scale `d_N` in the index-one
regular-variation theorem.  The asymptotic clock is
`c_(N,β) ∼ d_N * speedTiltCollisionScaleCoefficient β`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.speedTiltRawMergerCoefficient
definitions.body: speedTiltCollisionScaleCoefficient β * speedTiltBetaMergerRate β b k
definitions.docstring: Raw merger coefficient on the `d_N` timescale before pair-rate normalization.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.speedTiltPairCollisionScale
definitions.docstring:
Pair-collision asymptotic at tail scale `d`. In the index-one regular-variation theorem
this represents `c_(N,β) ∼ d_N / (β + 1)`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.speedTiltTwoFamilyCollisionScale
definitions.docstring:
Two-family pair-pair collision asymptotic at tail scale `d`. Its quadratic dependence on
`d` is the mechanism excluding simultaneous disjoint mergers from the limiting coalescent.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.speedBiasParameterFromTripleRate
definitions.docstring: Parameter readout from the normalized three-lineage rate.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.frontSpeedBiasParameter
definitions.docstring: Speed tilt after a front-displacement scale `γ`: the genealogy sees `θ / γ`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.frontSpeedTiltFromTripleRate
definitions.docstring:
Front-speed tilt reconstructed from an observed normalized triple-merger rate and a known
positive displacement scale.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.bolthausenSznitmanTotalMergerRate
definitions.docstring:
Telescoping collision-rate sum with `n + 1` active blocks.  For the uniform merger law,
the total rate contributed by mergers of every possible size is this sum: the multiplicity
times the rate for size `j + 2` reduces to
`(n + 1) (1 / (j + 1) - 1 / (j + 2))`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.criticallyPulledLinearRateLadder
definitions.docstring:
Canonical positive linear ladder representing a critically pulled total collision rate.
The normalized `Beta(1, β + 1)` family has this order with coefficient `β + 1`; the analytic
identification of that coefficient is separate from the summability argument.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.stablePowerRateLadder
definitions.docstring:
Canonical power-law ladder for an `α`-stable semipushed genealogy.  Multiplying this by a
positive constant, such as `1 / Γ(α+1)`, does not change reciprocal summability.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM; this is the comparison sequence used to formalize
the reciprocal-rate summability boundary.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.NormVisibility.rootMeanSquare
definitions.body: Real.sqrt ((∑ coordinate, perturbation coordinate ^ 2) / (Fintype.card Coordinate : ℝ))
definitions.docstring:
The **mean-square size** of a perturbation: its Euclidean norm divided by the square
root of the number of coordinates, so that a perturbation of constant amplitude has this
size equal to that amplitude regardless of how many coordinates there are. This is the
size a population-average second-moment statistic reports.

With no coordinates the division is by zero and Mathlib returns `0`; there is no mean
square of an empty population, and `rootMeanSquare_of_isEmpty` records the junk value
rather than leaving it to be discovered.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.NormVisibility.supremumNorm
definitions.docstring:
The **worst-case size** of a perturbation: the largest absolute coordinate. This is
the size a per-individual audit reports.

With no coordinates the supremum is over an empty family and Mathlib returns `0`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.NormVisibility.supportSize
definitions.docstring: The number of coordinates a perturbation actually moves.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.NormVisibility.localizedFamily
definitions.body: fun coordinate ↦ if (coordinate : ℕ) = 0 then 1 else 0
definitions.docstring:
The **localized family**: unit amplitude on the first coordinate, zero elsewhere. At
dimension zero it is the empty function, which is the honest reading — there is no first
coordinate — and the statements below all carry a positivity premise.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.NormVisibility.denseFamily
definitions.docstring: The **dense family**: unit amplitude on every coordinate.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.NormVisibility.WorstCaseVisible
definitions.signature: (family : ∀ dimension : ℕ, Fin dimension → ℝ) : Prop
definitions.body: ∃ floor : ℝ, 0 < floor ∧ ∀ᶠ dimension in atTop, floor ≤ supremumNorm (family dimension)
definitions.docstring:
A family is **worst-case visible** when some fixed positive amplitude survives in its
largest coordinate at every large dimension: a per-individual audit keeps finding it.

hypotheses: ∀ᶠ dimension in atTop, ∃ coordinate, |family dimension coordinate| = 1

Descent.Blindness.NormVisibility.worstCa: ∀ᶠ dimension in atTop, ∃ coordinate, |family dimension coordinate| = 1

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.NormVisibility.MeanSquareVisible
definitions.signature: (family : ∀ dimension : ℕ, Fin dimension → ℝ) : Prop
definitions.body: ∃ floor : ℝ, 0 < floor ∧ ∀ᶠ dimension in atTop, floor ≤ rootMeanSquare (family dimension)
definitions.docstring:
A family is **mean-square visible** when some fixed positive amplitude survives in its
population average at every large dimension: a pooled second-moment statistic keeps finding
it.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.NormVisibility.SupportVisible
definitions.signature: (family : ∀ dimension : ℕ, Fin dimension → ℝ) : Prop
definitions.body:
∃ fraction : ℝ, 0 < fraction ∧ ∀ᶠ dimension : ℕ in atTop,
    fraction * (dimension : ℝ) ≤ (supportSize (family dimension) : ℝ)
definitions.docstring:
A family is **support visible** when it moves a fixed positive fraction of the
coordinates at every large dimension: it is broad, whatever its amplitude.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.ProbeBlindness.and
definitions.signature: {D₁ D₂ : Type*} {p₁ : Object → D₁} {p₂ : Object → D₂} {P : Object → Prop} (B₁ : ProbeBlindness p₁ P) (B₂ : ProbeBlindness p₂ P) (hpos : B₂.positive = B₁.positive) (hneg : B₂.negative = B₁.negative) : ProbeBlindness (fun o ↦ (p₁ o, p₂ o)) P where positive
definitions.ret_type: ProbeBlindness (fun o ↦ (p₁ o, p₂ o)) P where positive
definitions.body:
B₁.positive
  negative := B₁.negative
  same_data := by
    have h₂ : p₂ B₁.positive = p₂ B₁.negative := by
      rw [← hpos, ← hneg]; exact B₂.same_data
    rw [B₁.same_data, h₂]
  holds := B₁.holds
  fails := B₁.fails
definitions.docstring:
**Two probes with a shared witness pair combine into a blind probe.** Running both
checks and reading the pair of answers is no better than running either.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.ProbeBlindness.ofWitnessFamily
definitions.signature: {Data ι : Type*} (p : ι → Object → Data) (P : Object → Prop) (pos neg : Object) (hsame : ∀ i, p i pos = p i neg) (hpos : P pos) (hneg : ¬ P neg) : ProbeBlindness (fun o ↦ fun i ↦ p i o) P where positive

args.type: ∀ i, p i pos = p i neg

definitions.ret_type: ProbeBlindness (fun o ↦ fun i ↦ p i o) P where positive
definitions.body:
pos
  negative := neg
  same_data := by funext i; exact hsame i
  holds := hpos
  fails := hneg
definitions.docstring:
**A single witness pair blinds an entire family of probes at once.**

This is the general form: give one pair of objects that every member of the family
reports identically on, and no criterion reading the whole family — in any combination,
by any rule — decides the property. A guard suite is exactly such a family.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.ObservationalSymmetry.toProbeBlindness
definitions.signature: (S : ObservationalSymmetry observe target) (P : Parameter → Prop) (hpositive : P (S.transform S.moved)) (hnegative : ¬ P S.moved) : ProbeBlindness observe P where positive
definitions.body:
S.transform S.moved
  negative := S.moved
  same_data := S.observation_invariant S.moved
  holds := hpositive
  fails := hnegative
definitions.docstring:
**A symmetry is a blindness witness.** Any property the transformation flips at the
moved parameter is undecidable from the observation, by `no_criterion_of_factors`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.ObservationalSymmetry.targetBlindness
definitions.signature: (S : ObservationalSymmetry observe target) : ProbeBlindness observe (fun parameter ↦ target parameter = target (S.transform S.moved))
definitions.ret_type: ProbeBlindness observe (fun parameter ↦ target parameter = target (S.transform S.moved))
definitions.docstring:
The canonical instance: the property *"the target takes the value it takes after the
transformation"* is flipped by construction, so no hypothesis is needed.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.ApproxProbeBlindness.witness
definitions.signature: : ApproxProbeBlindness (fun _ _ : Unit ↦ True) (fun _ : Bool ↦ ()) (fun b ↦ b = true) where positive
definitions.ret_type: ApproxProbeBlindness (fun _ _ : Unit ↦ True) (fun _ : Bool ↦ ()) (fun b ↦ b = true) where positive
definitions.body:
true
  negative := false
  close_data := trivial
  holds := rfl
  fails := by decide
definitions.docstring:
**The class is inhabited.**  A theorem quantified over an uninhabited structure is
true and empty: kernel-checked, clean axiom report, no content.  This is the witness that
makes the theorems below statements about something.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.LeveledBlindness.witness
definitions.signature: : LeveledBlindness (fun (_ : Unit) (_ : Bool) ↦ ()) (fun b ↦ b = true) where positive
definitions.ret_type: LeveledBlindness (fun (_ : Unit) (_ : Bool) ↦ ()) (fun b ↦ b = true) where positive
definitions.body:
true
  negative := false
  same_data := fun _ ↦ rfl
  holds := rfl
  fails := by decide
definitions.docstring:
**The class is inhabited.**  A theorem quantified over an uninhabited structure is
true and empty: kernel-checked, clean axiom report, no content.  This is the witness that
makes the theorems below statements about something.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.LeveledBlindness.toProbeBlindness
definitions.signature: (B : LeveledBlindness probe P) : ProbeBlindness (fun o ↦ fun ℓ ↦ probe ℓ o) P where positive
definitions.ret_type: ProbeBlindness (fun o ↦ fun ℓ ↦ probe ℓ o) P where positive
definitions.body:
B.positive
  negative := B.negative
  same_data := by funext ℓ; exact B.same_data ℓ
  holds := B.holds
  fails := B.fails
definitions.docstring: Collapse a leveled witness to a single-level witness for the full-family probe.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.LeveledBlindness.atLevel
definitions.signature: (B : LeveledBlindness probe P) (ℓ : Level) : ProbeBlindness (probe ℓ) P where positive
definitions.body:
B.positive
  negative := B.negative
  same_data := B.same_data ℓ
  holds := B.holds
  fails := B.fails
definitions.docstring: Blindness at a single level, for each level.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.IsCompleteCatalogue
definitions.signature: {α Invariant : Type*} (E : α → α → Prop) (label : α → Invariant) : Prop
definitions.body: ∀ x y, E x y ↔ label x = label y
definitions.docstring:
A **catalogue** for an equivalence relation is an assignment of invariants that is
complete: equal labels exactly when equivalent.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.IsUnionOfCertificates
definitions.signature: {α ι : Type*} (E : α → α → Prop) (cert : ι → α → α → Prop) : Prop
definitions.body: ∀ x y, E x y ↔ ∃ c : ι, cert c x y
definitions.docstring:
The **shape** statement, named for what it actually says: `E` is the union of the
family `cert`. This is a real and useful shape — it is what `boundedLogDistortion` and
the bounded-radius audits establish — but on its own it is not a ceiling, and the name
must not claim one.

hypotheses: ∀ x y, E x y ↔ F (f x

Descent.Blindness.unionOfCertificates_of: ∀ x y, E x y ↔ F (f x

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.ProbeSeparation.witness
definitions.body:
1
  sigma_pos := by norm_num
  separates := fun _ _ ↦ by simp
definitions.docstring:
**The class is inhabited.**  A theorem quantified over an uninhabited structure is
true and empty: kernel-checked, clean axiom report, no content.  This is the witness that
makes the theorems below statements about something.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.duplicate_separation
definitions.signature: {Object : Type*} [MetricSpace Object] (f : Object → ℝ) (S : ProbeSeparation f) : ProbeSeparation (fun o ↦ ((f o, f o) : ℝ × ℝ)) where sigma
definitions.ret_type: ProbeSeparation (fun o ↦ ((f o, f o) : ℝ × ℝ)) where sigma
definitions.body:
S.sigma
  sigma_pos := S.sigma_pos
  separates := by
    intro o o'
    rw [duplicate_dist]
    exact S.separates o o'
definitions.docstring:
**Duplicating a channel buys no separation.** The modulus of the doubled probe is the
modulus of the original, so a perfectly redundant coordinate contributes nothing to
resolving objects.

Declared `def` rather than `theorem`: `ProbeSeparation` is a STRUCTURE carrying a real
modulus, so this returns data, not a proof, and `theorem` requires a `Prop`. Declaring it
`theorem` makes the elaborator report "type of theorem
`Descent.duplicate_separation` is not a proposition". The keyword is the only thing at
stake, since the body builds the witness with `where` either way. Keeping it as data is
also strictly stronger than the
`Nonempty (ProbeSeparation _)` a `theorem` forces: the duplicated probe's
modulus is available, and `duplicate_separation f S |>.sigma` is definitionally
`S.sigma`, which is the content the surrounding prose claims.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.atomicRechopping
definitions.docstring:
**Atomic re-chopping**: keep the semantics, replace the storage by one node per semantic
coordinate. This is the canonical representative of a graph's rewrite class.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.rechoppingSymmetry
definitions.signature: : ObservationalSymmetry (fun graph : GraphPresentation (Fin 2) ↦ classOf graph) (fun graph : GraphPresentation (Fin 2) ↦ graphNodeCount graph) where transform
definitions.ret_type: ObservationalSymmetry (fun graph : GraphPresentation (Fin 2) ↦ classOf graph) (fun graph : GraphPresentation (Fin 2) ↦ graphNodeCount graph) where transform
definitions.body:
atomicRechopping
  observation_invariant := classOf_atomicRechopping
  moved := mergedNodeWitness
  target_moved := by
    intro hcount
    norm_num [atomicRechopping, graphNodeCount, splitNodeWitness, mergedNodeWitness,
      atomicGraph, discretePresentation] at hcount
definitions.docstring:
**Re-chopping is an observational symmetry of the pangenome, with the node count as its
moved target.**

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.pushedCumulantTensor
definitions.signature: (order : ℕ) (mixing : Matrix Row Locus ℝ) (kappa : ℝ) (indices : Fin order → Row) : ℝ
definitions.body: kappa * ∑ locus, ∏ leg, mixing (indices leg) locus
definitions.docstring:
Order-`q` cumulant tensor obtained by mixing independent coordinates with common scalar
cumulant `kappa`.  Indexing tensor legs by `Fin q` makes the construction uniform in `q`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.cumulantTensorEnergy
definitions.docstring: Squared Frobenius norm of an arbitrary-order tensor.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.entryPowerSum
definitions.signature: (covariance : Matrix Locus Locus ℝ) (order : ℕ) : ℝ
definitions.body: ∑ left, ∑ right, covariance left right ^ order
definitions.docstring:
The two-vertex, `order`-parallel-edge traffic observable.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM. The sum is algebra on a covariance matrix: given
the matrix, the number is determined, and no population can make it come out otherwise. The
empirical claim in its neighbourhood -- that this quantity separates LD matrices the
spectrum cannot tell apart -- is proved below on explicit witnesses, which is a stronger
settlement than a simulation would give, since a witness pair exhibits the separation rather
than estimating it.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.pushedThirdMomentTensor
definitions.signature: (mixing : Matrix Row Locus ℝ) (kappa : ℝ) (a b c : Row) : ℝ
definitions.body: kappa * ∑ i, mixing a i * mixing b i * mixing c i
definitions.docstring:
The third moment tensor obtained by applying `mixing` to independent centered coordinates
whose common scalar third moment is `kappa`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.thirdTensorEnergy
definitions.body: ∑ a, ∑ b, ∑ c, tensor a b c ^ 2
definitions.docstring: Squared Frobenius norm of a three-index tensor.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.entryCubeSum
definitions.docstring:
The first non-spectral invariant seen by a skewed product prior: the sum of the cubes of all
entries of a covariance matrix.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.gramCovariance
definitions.signature: (mixing : Matrix Row Locus ℝ) : Matrix Locus Locus ℝ
definitions.docstring: The Gram covariance induced by a mixing matrix.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.pushedFourthCumulantTensor
definitions.signature: (mixing : Matrix Row Locus ℝ) (kappa : ℝ) (a b c d : Row) : ℝ
definitions.body: kappa * ∑ i, mixing a i * mixing b i * mixing c i * mixing d i
definitions.docstring:
The fourth cumulant tensor obtained by applying `mixing` to independent centered
coordinates whose common scalar fourth cumulant is `kappa`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.fourthTensorEnergy
definitions.signature: (tensor : Row → Row → Row → Row → ℝ) : ℝ
definitions.body: ∑ a, ∑ b, ∑ c, ∑ d, tensor a b c d ^ 2
definitions.docstring: Squared Frobenius norm of a four-index tensor.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.entryFourthSum
definitions.docstring:
The orientation-sensitive invariant that remains available to symmetric non-Gaussian
product priors: the sum of the fourth powers of all covariance entries.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.ldPowerScore
definitions.signature: (covariance : Matrix Locus Locus ℝ) (power : ℕ) (j : Locus) : ℝ
definitions.docstring:
The power-`power` LD score of one locus.  Power two is the usual LD score; power four is
the per-locus statistic detecting symmetric non-Gaussian orientation effects.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM. Like `entryPowerSum`, the body is a column sum of
matrix entries raised to a power: given the LD matrix the number is determined. Power two is
the standard LD score and is measured routinely elsewhere; the fourth-power statistic named
here has not been computed on any panel in this development, and nothing below claims it
has. What would be empirical is a claim about the VALUE this statistic takes on real LD --
that no definition in this file makes.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.localizedCovarianceBlock
definitions.docstring: A covariance block localized in the product-prior coordinate basis.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.rotatedCovarianceBlock
definitions.docstring: The same covariance eigenvalues after a forty-five degree rotation.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.Isospectral2
definitions.body:
∀ spectralParameter : ℝ,
    Matrix.det (left - spectralParameter • 1) =
      Matrix.det (right - spectralParameter • 1)
definitions.docstring:
Exact isospectrality for two-dimensional matrices, expressed without choosing or ordering
eigenvectors: their characteristic determinants agree at every spectral parameter.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.blockEntryCubeMean
definitions.docstring: Per-coordinate normalization of the entrywise cube invariant for a two-dimensional block.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.blockEntryFourthMean
definitions.docstring: Per-coordinate normalization of the entrywise fourth-power invariant for a block.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.localizedUniformFourthInvariant
definitions.docstring:
Per-coordinate fourth-order invariant of the localized block family, averaged uniformly
over offsets `a ∈ [1, 2]`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.rotatedUniformFourthInvariant
definitions.docstring:
Per-coordinate fourth-order invariant of the rotated block family, averaged uniformly over
offsets `a ∈ [1, 2]`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.lowSNRFourthOrientationCoefficient
definitions.docstring: The orientation-sensitive part of the fourth low-SNR mutual-information coefficient.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.gaussianDesignFourthSpectralMoment
definitions.signature: (c m1 m2 m3 m4 : ℝ) : ℝ
definitions.docstring:
The fourth spectral moment produced by the rectangular Gaussian design.  Here `c` is the
inverse aspect ratio and `m1`, ..., `m4` are the first four covariance spectral moments.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.lowSNRFourthCoefficient
definitions.signature: (c variance fourthCumulant m1 m2 m3 m4 h4 : ℝ) : ℝ
definitions.body:
-(variance ^ 4 / 8 * gaussianDesignFourthSpectralMoment c m1 m2 m3 m4) -
    fourthCumulant ^ 2 / 48 * h4
definitions.docstring:
Complete fourth low-SNR coefficient: a spectral Wishart term plus the fourth-cumulant
traffic term.  This definition keeps the two information channels visibly separate.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.entrySquareSum
definitions.signature: {Locus : Type*} [Fintype Locus] (covariance : Matrix Locus Locus ℝ) : ℝ
definitions.docstring: Entrywise square sum, the two-parallel-edge traffic observable.

hypotheses: ∀ i j, covariance j i = covariance i j

Descent.Blindness.entrySquareSum_eq_trac: ∀ i j, covariance j i = covariance i j

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.centeredSparsePriorAtom
definitions.docstring:
Three equiprobable atoms realizing the centered form of the sparse prior
`(2 / 3) delta_(-1) + (1 / 3) delta_2`.  Repeating `-1` twice avoids introducing a
measure-theoretic wrapper around an elementary finite law.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.lowSNRThirdCoefficient
definitions.signature: (aspect variance thirdMoment m1 m2 m3 h3 : ℝ) : ℝ
definitions.body:
variance ^ 3 / 6 *
      (m3 + 3 * m1 * m2 / aspect + m1 ^ 3 / aspect ^ 2) -
    thirdMoment ^ 2 / 12 * h3
definitions.docstring:
The cubic low-SNR coefficient after the spectral terms and the orientation term are
separated.  `m1`, `m2`, and `m3` are spectral moments; `h3` is the entrywise-cube invariant.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.ldOrientationInvariant
definitions.signature: {Locus : Type*} [Fintype Locus] (order : ℕ) (ld : Matrix Locus Locus ℝ) : ℝ
definitions.docstring:
The order-`q` orientation-sensitive LD traffic invariant in the locus coordinate basis.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM. A renaming of `entryPowerSum` in biological
vocabulary, carrying that definition's status: algebra on a given matrix, with no panel
computation behind it and none needed, since the value follows from the matrix.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.ldOrientationThirdInvariant
definitions.signature: {Locus : Type*} [Fintype Locus] (ld : Matrix Locus Locus ℝ) : ℝ
definitions.docstring:
The orientation-sensitive third-order LD invariant in the locus coordinate basis.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM, as for `ldOrientationInvariant`: algebra on the LD
matrix, never evaluated on a real one here and not the kind of thing a real one could
contradict.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.ldOrientationFourthInvariant
definitions.signature: {Locus : Type*} [Fintype Locus] (ld : Matrix Locus Locus ℝ) : ℝ
definitions.docstring:
The orientation-sensitive fourth-order LD invariant in the locus coordinate basis.  It is
the summed fourth-power LD score and remains visible for symmetric sparse effect priors.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM. The body is the summed fourth-power LD score, a
function of the matrix alone. "Remains visible" is proved on the explicit witness pair
below, at one dimension and one prior; it is not a measurement on genotype data, and a
witness settles a separation more firmly than a measurement of it would.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.SpectrumIdentifiability.LinearTargetDeterminedByObservation
definitions.signature: {R V W Z : Type*} [Ring R] [AddCommGroup V] [Module R V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module R W] [AddCommGroup Z] [Module R Z] (observation : V →ₗ[R] W) (target : V →ₗ[R] Z) : Prop
definitions.body: ∀ left right, observation left = observation right → target left = target right
definitions.docstring:
A derived linear target is determined by an observation when it is constant on every
observation fiber. This is weaker than identifying the full input and is the right notion for
questions such as whether a particular demographic average is recoverable from the SFS.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.SpectrumIdentifiability.spectrumAttenuation
definitions.body: ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, Real.exp (-(2 * Coalescent.deathRate (k + 2) * τ))
definitions.docstring:
Squared spectral energy an epoch-localised perturbation can still deposit, when it is
supported after cumulative coalescent time `τ`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.SpectrumIdentifiability.cauchyConditioningProfile
definitions.body:
2 * (Real.log (1 + θ ^ 2) + (θ - 1) * Real.log (1 - θ)
    - (1 + θ) * Real.log (1 + θ) + 2 * θ * Real.arctan (1 / θ))
definitions.docstring:
Cauchy-matrix conditioning profile, in the form whose singularities cancel.

The literal integrand `log ((θ² + x²) / |θ² - x²|)` integrates to
`2 [log ((1 + θ²) / (1 - θ²)) + 2θ arctan (1/θ) -
θ log ((1 + θ) / (1 - θ))]`, where the two divergent logarithms cancel as `θ → 1`.
The regrouping below performs that cancellation symbolically, so the profile is finite on
all of `[0, 1]`.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM. This is the closed form of an
integral, checked by the theorems below rather than by measurement: an integral
either equals its closed form or does not, and no population bears on which.
The conditioning of the Cauchy matrix it carries IS numerically measurable, but
that is a property of a computation rather than of this identity, and it belongs
to whatever definition states it.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.SpectrumIdentifiability.CauchyConditioningStationary
definitions.docstring:
Exact transcendental stationarity equation for the Cauchy conditioning profile.  Its
right side is `artanh θ`, written in logarithmic form because Mathlib has no separate real
inverse-hyperbolic-tangent API.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.SpectrumIdentifiability.stableSieveDimension
definitions.docstring:
Largest sieve dimension whose spectral direction is still resolvable at genome length `L`,
when the Laplace core's smallest singular value decays like `exp (-κ r / 2)`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.cwRate
definitions.body: (1 + m) / 2 * Real.log (1 + m) + (1 - m) / 2 * Real.log (1 - m)
definitions.docstring:
The Curie-Weiss rate function for a balanced Rademacher magnetisation.

    Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM. This is the Cramer rate function of
    a fair coin, fixed by that description alone; no measurement bears on it.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.cwObjective
definitions.docstring:
The quantity whose supremum over `m` is the overlap-pressure gap.

    Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.cwPinskerGap
definitions.docstring: Pinsker gap for the balanced Bernoulli pair.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.cwPinskerGapDerivative
definitions.docstring: Derivative of the Pinsker gap on the open magnetisation interval.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.cwPressureValueSet
definitions.docstring:
Values attained by the Curie--Weiss variational objective on the admissible
magnetisation interval.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.cwVariationalPressureGap
definitions.docstring:
The actual variational pressure gap, rather than only its pointwise
objective.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.finiteCWMagnetization
definitions.docstring:
Magnetisation of the type with `upSpins` positive spins in a population of
size `population`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.finiteCWEmpiricalMagnetization
definitions.docstring: Magnetisation density of one finite Rademacher type.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.cwPositiveTrialWeight
definitions.docstring:
Positive-spin probability in the biased Rademacher trial law associated
with magnetisation `m`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.cwNegativeTrialWeight
definitions.docstring: Negative-spin probability in the same trial law.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.biasedBinomialTypeWeight
definitions.body:
(Nat.choose population upSpins : ℝ) *
    q ^ upSpins * r ^ (population - upSpins)
definitions.docstring:
Binomial type weight under a trial product law with positive-spin weight
`q` and negative-spin weight `r`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.finiteCWPartition
definitions.body:
((2 : ℝ) ^ population)⁻¹ *
    ∑ upSpins ∈ Finset.range (population + 1),
      (Nat.choose population upSpins : ℝ) *
        Real.exp
          (tlam / (2 * (population : ℝ)) *
            finiteCWMagnetization population upSpins ^ 2)
definitions.docstring:
The exact Curie--Weiss/Rademacher partition function after dividing by the
`2^population` configurations.  Grouping configurations by their number of
positive spins produces the binomial coefficient in the sum.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.finiteCWPressureGap
definitions.docstring: Normalized finite-volume pressure difference from the unspiked baseline.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.finiteCWTypeMass
definitions.body:
((2 : ℝ) ^ population)⁻¹ *
    (Nat.choose population upSpins : ℝ) *
      Real.exp
        (tlam / (2 * (population : ℝ)) *
          finiteCWMagnetization population upSpins ^ 2)
definitions.docstring:
Contribution of one magnetisation type to the normalized finite
Curie--Weiss partition function.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.finiteBaselineRademacherPressure
definitions.docstring:
The unspiked `aI` contribution to the normalized one-replica quadratic
Rademacher pressure.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.finiteRankOneRademacherPressure
definitions.body:
finiteBaselineRademacherPressure baseline temperature +
    finiteCWPressureGap population (temperature * spikeStrength)

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.FiniteRankOnePressureCriticalStatement
definitions.body:
Filter.Tendsto
      (fun population : ℕ ↦
        finiteRankOneRademacherPressure baseline (population + 1)
            temperature spikeStrength -
          finiteBaselineRademacherPressure baseline temperature)
      Filter.atTop (nhds 0) ↔
    temperature * spikeStrength ≤ 1
definitions.docstring: The exact-criticality statement for the finite rank-one pressure sequence.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.FiniteRankOnePressureVariationalLimitStatement
definitions.body:
Filter.Tendsto
    (fun population : ℕ ↦
      finiteRankOneRademacherPressure baseline (population + 1)
        temperature spikeStrength)
    Filter.atTop
    (nhds (finiteBaselineRademacherPressure baseline temperature +
      cwVariationalPressureGap (temperature * spikeStrength)))
definitions.docstring: The variational-limit statement for the complete finite rank-one pressure.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.FiniteRankOnePressureUniformLimitStatement
definitions.body:
TendstoUniformlyOn
    (fun population : ℕ ↦ fun spikeStrength : ℝ ↦
      finiteRankOneRademacherPressure baseline (population + 1)
        temperature spikeStrength)
    (fun spikeStrength ↦
      finiteBaselineRademacherPressure baseline temperature +
        cwVariationalPressureGap (temperature * spikeStrength))
    Filter.atTop (Set.Ici 0)
definitions.docstring: The uniform nonnegative-spike convergence statement.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.RankOneSpikeInvisibleWithFinitePressure
definitions.signature: {Term : Type*} [Fintype Term] (coefficient : Term → ℝ) (hasOddDegree : Term → Bool) (vertices edges : Term → ℕ) (tlam : ℝ) : Prop
definitions.body:
Filter.Tendsto
      (fun population : ℕ ↦
        finiteRankOneTrafficCorrection coefficient hasOddDegree vertices edges
          (population + 1))
      Filter.atTop (nhds 0) ∧
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun population : ℕ ↦ finiteCWPressureGap (population + 1) tlam)
      Filter.atTop (nhds (cwVariationalPressureGap tlam)) ∧
    ∃ m : ℝ, |m| < 1 ∧ 0 < cwObjective tlam m ∧
      (∀ population : ℕ,
        cwObjective tlam m ≤ finiteCWPressureGap (population + 1) tlam) ∧
      ¬ Filter.Tendsto
        (fun population : ℕ ↦ finiteCWPressureGap (population + 1) tlam)
        Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
definitions.docstring:
**The finite-volume properties one rank-one spike has at once**, as one
proposition: every fixed traffic correction vanishes, the genuine pressure
converges to the variational value, and one positive interior witness uniformly
lower-bounds every finite pressure, so that pressure cannot vanish
asymptotically.

Named for the same reason as `RankOneSpikeRefutesBothDichotomies`: the theorem that proves
it, the genomic restatement that cites that theorem, and the obstruction registry each
carried the conjunction in full, so a change to one copy would have been a silent divergence
rather than a build error.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM. This names four propositions, each
proved below at finite volume on an explicit spike, so there is no measurement
that could agree or disagree with it. What a measurement could bear on is
whether a real LD spike is rank-one, which nothing here asserts. An UNTESTED
marker would read as a measurement owed, and none is.

hypotheses: ∀ term, hasOddDegree term = false → vertices term ≤ edges term

Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSepara: ∀ term, hasOddDegree term = false → vertices term ≤ edges term
Descent.Conditionals.positiveLDSpike_fix: ∀ term, hasOddDegree term = false → vertices term ≤ edges term

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.RankOneSpikeRefutesBothDichotomies
definitions.signature: {Term Spin : Type*} [Fintype Term] (coefficient : Term → ℝ) (hasOddDegree : Term → Bool) (vertices edges : Term → ℕ) (alignment : Spin → ℝ) (orthogonal aligned : Spin) (baseline spikeStrength population temperature : ℝ) : Prop
definitions.body:
Filter.Tendsto
      (fun size : ℕ ↦
        finiteRankOneTrafficCorrection coefficient hasOddDegree vertices edges (size + 1))
      Filter.atTop (nhds 0) ∧
    (∀ state, baseline ≤
      rankOneEnergyDensity baseline spikeStrength population (alignment state)) ∧
    rankOneEnergyDensity baseline spikeStrength population (alignment orthogonal) =
      baseline ∧
    baseline <
      rankOneEnergyDensity baseline spikeStrength population (alignment aligned) ∧
    0 < cwVariationalPressureGap (temperature * spikeStrength)
definitions.docstring:
**The four properties one positive rank-one spike has at once**, as one proposition.

The theorem below establishes it, `DynamicsContrast` restates it in genomic vocabulary and
cites that theorem, and the obstruction registry carries it as a field.  Written out, the
conjunction stood in the corpus three times, and a change to any one copy would have been a
silent divergence between them rather than a build error.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM. This names a conjunction of four
propositions, each proved below on an explicit spike, so there is no measurement
that could agree or disagree with it. What a measurement could bear on is
whether a real LD spike is rank-one, which nothing here asserts. An UNTESTED
marker would read as a measurement owed, and none is.

hypotheses: ∀ term, hasOddDegree term = false → vertices term ≤ edges term

Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSepara: ∀ term, hasOddDegree term = false → vertices term ≤ edges term
Descent.Conditionals.positiveLDSpike_ref: ∀ term, hasOddDegree term = false → vertices term ≤ edges term

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.algorithmicRiskSignature
definitions.signature: {Algorithm Design Model Loss : Type*} (risk : Algorithm → Design → Model → Loss → ℝ) (design : Design) : Algorithm → Model → Loss → ℝ
definitions.body: fun algorithm model loss ↦ risk algorithm design model loss
definitions.docstring:
The complete limiting-risk signature of a design for a uniform procedure class.  Algorithms,
models, and losses are all arguments, so a procedure cannot contain the design identity as
nonuniform advice.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.AlgorithmicallyEquivalent
definitions.signature: {Algorithm Design Model Loss : Type*} (risk : Algorithm → Design → Model → Loss → ℝ) (left right : Design) : Prop
definitions.body: ∀ algorithm model loss, risk algorithm left model loss = risk algorithm right model loss
definitions.docstring:
Two designs are indistinguishable by the entire uniform class exactly when all entries of
their limiting-risk signatures agree.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.RiskSignaturesFactorThrough
definitions.signature: {Algorithm Design Model Loss Invariant : Type*} (risk : Algorithm → Design → Model → Loss → ℝ) (invariant : Design → Invariant) : Prop
definitions.body:
∃ reconstruct : Invariant → Algorithm → Model → Loss → ℝ,
    ∀ design,
      reconstruct (invariant design) = algorithmicRiskSignature risk design
definitions.docstring:
All risks of the uniform procedure class factor through a proposed design
invariant when one common reconstruction map recovers the complete risk
signature from that invariant.  Requiring a common map is what excludes
nonuniform design advice.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.separationBlindness
definitions.signature: {Design Invariant : Type*} (invariant : Design → Invariant) (bayes : Design → ℝ) (d d' : Design) (thr : ℝ) (same : invariant d = invariant d') (hd : bayes d ≤ thr) (hd' : ¬ bayes d' ≤ thr) : ProbeBlindness invariant (fun x ↦ bayes x ≤ thr) where positive
definitions.ret_type: ProbeBlindness invariant (fun x ↦ bayes x ≤ thr) where positive
definitions.body:
d
  negative := d'
  same_data := same
  holds := hd
  fails := hd'
definitions.docstring:
**An invariant separation is an instance of the observational ceiling.**

    `Descent.Blindness.ObservationalCeiling` states the law this file's template is a
    quantitative form of: a probe returning the same data on two objects
    certifies neither, so no criterion factoring through it decides any property
    separating them. Here the probe is the algorithmic invariant, and the
    property is "the optimum is at least as good as `thr`".

    Relating the two is what makes this module contradictable from outside it: if
    the separation pair were wrong, `ProbeBlindness.no_criterion` would deliver a
    false conclusion about the corpus's own blindness law rather than only about
    a private definition here.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.zeroFiniteLowRankSingularSpectrum
definitions.signature: (Coordinate : Type*) [Fintype Coordinate] : FiniteLowRankSingularSpectrum Coordinate where singularValue
definitions.body:
fun _coordinate ↦ 0
  active := ∅
  rank := 0
  operatorBound := 0
  operatorBound_nonnegative := le_rfl
  singularValue_nonnegative := by simp
  singularValue_le_operatorBound := by simp
  inactive_zero := by simp
  active_card_le_rank := by simp
definitions.docstring:
The zero spectrum is a concrete inhabitant of the low-rank certificate
type; its support, rank, and operator bound all vanish.

Stated at an arbitrary finite coordinate type rather than at `PUnit`, because
what it is for is `finiteLowRankSingularSpectrum_nonempty` just below: every
result in this section is universally quantified over
`FiniteLowRankSingularSpectrum Coordinate`, and a universally quantified
statement about an uninhabited type is true for reasons that have nothing to do
with singular values. Pinning the witness to a one-point coordinate space would
have established non-vacuity at one dimension only, which is the dimension none
of the asymptotic results are about.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.FiniteLowRankSingularSpectrum.rawNuclearDistance
definitions.docstring:
Raw nuclear distance represented by the sum of the certified singular

definitions.docstring: Dimension-normalized nuclear distance.

definitions.docstring: Dimension-normalized rank.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.finiteRankOneSingularSpectrum
definitions.signature: (population : ℕ) (spikeStrength : ℝ) (hspike : 0 ≤ spikeStrength) : FiniteLowRankSingularSpectrum (FiniteOutlierCoordinate population) where singularValue | none => spikeStrength | some _coordinate => 0 active
definitions.ret_type: FiniteLowRankSingularSpectrum (FiniteOutlierCoordinate population) where singularValue | none => spikeStrength | some _coordinate => 0 active
definitions.body:
{none}
  rank := 1
  operatorBound := spikeStrength
  operatorBound_nonnegative := hspike
  singularValue_nonnegative := by
    intro coordinate
    cases coordinate <;> simp_all
  singularValue_le_operatorBound := by
    intro coordinate
    cases coordinate <;> simp_all
  inactive_zero := by
    intro coordinate hinactive
    cases coordinate with
    | none => simp at hinactive
    | some coordinate => rfl
  active_card_le_rank := by simp
definitions.docstring:
The concrete singular-value spectrum of a rank-one perturbation on the
`p+1`-dimensional outlier coordinate space.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.zeroMatchedInformationPathCertificate
definitions.body:
fun _interpolation ↦ 0
  tracePairing := fun _interpolation ↦ 0
  variance := 0
  nuclearDistance := 0
  variance_nonnegative := le_rfl
  nuclearDistance_nonnegative := le_rfl
  immseDerivative := by
    intro interpolation _hinterpolation
    simpa using (hasDerivAt_const interpolation (0 : ℝ)).hasDerivWithinAt
  posteriorCovarianceTraceBound := by simp
definitions.docstring:
The constant zero path is a concrete matched-information certificate.  It
anchors the abstract certificate API in an actual model with zero variance and
zero covariance displacement.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.saturatingMatchedInformationPathCertificate
definitions.signature: (variance nuclearDistance : ℝ) (hvariance : 0 ≤ variance) (hnuclear : 0 ≤ nuclearDistance) : MatchedInformationPathCertificate where informationPath
definitions.body:
fun interpolation ↦
    variance * nuclearDistance / 2 * interpolation
  tracePairing := fun _interpolation ↦ variance * nuclearDistance
  variance := variance
  nuclearDistance := nuclearDistance
  variance_nonnegative := hvariance
  nuclearDistance_nonnegative := hnuclear
  immseDerivative := by
    intro interpolation _hinterpolation
    have hderivative :
        HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ ↦ variance * nuclearDistance / 2 * t)
          (variance * nuclearDistance / 2) interpolation := by
      simpa using (hasDerivAt_id interpolation).const_mul
        (variance * nuclearDistance / 2)
    exact hderivative.hasDerivWithinAt
  posteriorCovarianceTraceBound := by
    intro _interpolation _hinterpolation
    exact le_of_eq (abs_of_nonneg (mul_nonneg hvariance hnuclear))
definitions.docstring:
**The certificate that runs at the maximum rate the trace bound allows.**
The information path is linear with slope `variance · nuclearDistance / 2`, and
the trace pairing sits at the boundary of `posteriorCovarianceTraceBound`
throughout.

`zeroMatchedInformationPathCertificate` is the degenerate member of this family,
at `variance = nuclearDistance = 0`; this is the family it is degenerate in.
Its purpose is `saturatingMatchedInformationPathCertificate_attains_bound`.

definitions.signature: {Index : Type*} (regime : Filter Index) (certificate : Index → MatchedInformationPathCertificate) : Prop

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.diagonalTrafficCorrection
definitions.docstring:
Difference between the diagonal traffic coordinate of `aI` and that of a diagonal matrix
whose exceptional fraction is `4⁻ᵏ` and exceptional value is `a + 2`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.MesoscopicGFOMCoordinate
definitions.docstring:
A concrete `16^k`-coordinate realization of the mesoscopic example.  The
second coordinate indexes `4^k` blocks; the exceptional subspace is the slice
whose second coordinate has value zero and therefore has exactly `4^k`
coordinates.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.MesoscopicGFOMExceptionalCoordinate
definitions.docstring: The exceptional coordinate slice supporting the amplified output.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.mesoscopicGFOMStep
definitions.signature: (iteration : ℕ) (vector : MesoscopicGFOMCoordinate iteration → ℝ) : MesoscopicGFOMCoordinate iteration → ℝ
definitions.body: fun coordinate ↦ if coordinate.2.val = 0 then 2 * vector coordinate else 0
definitions.docstring:
The actual diagonal GFOM step `(M-aI)x`: multiply the exceptional slice
by two and annihilate the bulk.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.mesoscopicGFOMIterate
definitions.signature: (iteration : ℕ) : ℕ → (MesoscopicGFOMCoordinate iteration → ℝ) → MesoscopicGFOMCoordinate iteration → ℝ
definitions.ret_type: ℕ → (MesoscopicGFOMCoordinate iteration → ℝ) → MesoscopicGFOMCoordinate iteration → ℝ
definitions.body:
| 0, vector => vector
  | runtime + 1, vector =>
      mesoscopicGFOMStep iteration (mesoscopicGFOMIterate iteration runtime vector)
definitions.docstring: Repeated application of the concrete diagonal step.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.mesoscopicGFOMUnitInput
definitions.docstring:
Deterministic unit input used to expose the exact normalized amplification
without adding an unnecessary probabilistic layer.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.mesoscopicGFOMActualEnergy
definitions.body:
(∑ coordinate : MesoscopicGFOMCoordinate iteration,
    mesoscopicGFOMIterate iteration runtime
      (mesoscopicGFOMUnitInput iteration) coordinate ^ 2) /
    (16 : ℝ) ^ iteration
definitions.docstring: Normalized squared output of the genuine finite diagonal iteration.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.mesoscopicGFOMEnergy
definitions.docstring:
Normalized squared output of the diagonal power iteration: the exceptional mass `4⁻ᵏ` is
amplified by `4ᵗ`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.FixedTrafficLogRuntimeSeparation
definitions.body:
(∀ edges : ℕ,
      Filter.Tendsto (fun iteration ↦ diagonalTrafficCorrection 1 edges iteration)
        Filter.atTop (nhds 0)) ∧
      ∀ iteration : ℕ, mesoscopicGFOMEnergy iteration iteration = 1
definitions.docstring: The fixed-coordinate/logarithmic-runtime separation contract.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.ConcreteGFOMLogRuntimeSeparation
definitions.body:
(∀ iteration : ℕ,
    Fintype.card (MesoscopicGFOMCoordinate iteration) = 16 ^ iteration ∧
      Fintype.card (MesoscopicGFOMExceptionalCoordinate iteration) = 4 ^ iteration) ∧
  (∀ edges : ℕ,
    Filter.Tendsto (fun iteration ↦ diagonalTrafficCorrection 1 edges iteration)
      Filter.atTop (nhds 0)) ∧
  (∀ runtime : ℕ,
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun iteration ↦ mesoscopicGFOMActualEnergy iteration (runtime + 1))
      Filter.atTop (nhds 0)) ∧
  ∀ iteration : ℕ, 0 < iteration →
    mesoscopicGFOMActualEnergy iteration iteration = 1
definitions.docstring: The concrete finite-matrix version of the logarithmic-runtime separation.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.amplifiedDegreeOneTrafficDifference
definitions.docstring:
A degree-one invariant polynomial may multiply its normalized trace
coordinate by a size-dependent coefficient.  On the `16^k`-dimensional
diagonal witness, the coefficient `4^k = p_k / r_k` exactly resolves the
exceptional block of relative mass `4⁻ᵏ`.

definitions.signature: {Slot Label : Type*} (left right : Slot → Label) : Prop
definitions.body: ∀ first second, left first = left second ↔ right first = right second
definitions.docstring:
Two endpoint-label assignments have the same equality pattern exactly when
they induce the same partition of the endpoint slots.  This relation is the
precise combinatorial content of having the same directed multigraph shape.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.EqualityPattern
definitions.docstring:
The canonical finite traffic-graph shape is the quotient of endpoint
assignments by equality pattern.  It records precisely a directed multigraph
with its ordered endpoint slots, and nothing about the particular labels.

definitions.signature: {Slot Label : Type*} (assignment : Slot → Label) : EqualityPattern Slot Label
definitions.docstring: Send an assignment to its canonical equality-pattern traffic shape.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.equalityPatternRangeEquiv
definitions.signature: {Slot Label : Type*} (left right : Slot → Label) (hpattern : SameEqualityPattern left right) : Set.range left ≃ Set.range right where toFun value
definitions.ret_type: Set.range left ≃ Set.range right where toFun value
definitions.body:
⟨right (Classical.choose value.property),
      ⟨Classical.choose value.property, rfl⟩⟩
  invFun value :=
    ⟨left (Classical.choose value.property),
      ⟨Classical.choose value.property, rfl⟩⟩
  left_inv value := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    have hleft := Classical.choose_spec value.property
    have hright := Classical.choose_spec
      ((⟨right (Classical.choose value.property),
        ⟨Classical.choose value.property, rfl⟩⟩ : Set.range right).property)
    exact (hpattern _ _).mpr (hright.trans rfl) |>.trans hleft
  right_inv value := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    have hright := Classical.choose_spec value.property
    have hleft := Classical.choose_spec
      ((⟨left (Classical.choose value.property),
        ⟨Classical.choose value.property, rfl⟩⟩ : Set.range left).property)
    exact (hpattern _ _).mp (hleft.trans rfl) |>.trans hright
definitions.docstring:
The occupied labels of two assignments with the same equality pattern are
equivalent: send the label at a slot on the left to the label at
the same slot on the right.  Choice only selects a representative slot; the
equality-pattern hypothesis proves the result independent of that choice.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.equalityPatternPermutation
definitions.signature: {Slot Label : Type*} [Finite Label] (left right : Slot → Label) (hpattern : SameEqualityPattern left right) : Equiv.Perm Label
definitions.body:
by
  classical
  exact Equiv.extendSubtype (equalityPatternRangeEquiv left right hpattern)
definitions.docstring:
On a finite label set, the equivalence between occupied labels extends to
a permutation of the entire label set.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.CanonicalTrafficFactorizationStatement
definitions.signature: {Slot Label : Type*} [Fintype Slot] [DecidableEq Slot] [Fintype Label] (coefficient value : (Slot → Label) → ℝ) : Prop

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.degreeAtMostCanonicalTrafficProfile

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.TruncatedTrafficRisk.totalTraffic
definitions.docstring:
**The total-traffic functional**: unit weight on every retained graph
coordinate.

`TruncatedTrafficRisk` had no exhibited inhabitant, so the stability bound below
was stated over an empty-for-all-we-knew class. This member also fixes the
orientation of the bound: its coefficient `ℓ¹` mass is the number of retained
coordinates, so the bound reads "degree controls the number of coordinates, and
therefore the amplification" on a functional where that is visible.

Convention: `D` is polynomial/edge degree, not the population-genetic
linkage-disequilibrium coefficient traditionally also denoted `D`. The two differ
by ploidy and nothing here is about haplotype frequencies; the same note is
carried by `TruncatedTrafficRisk.evaluate` above, and it is repeated rather than
cross-referenced because this definition takes the argument on its own.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.momentSeparationNode

annihilator of moments through degree `D`.

Convention: `D` is moment degree, not linkage-disequilibrium `D`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.momentPerturbationScale

Convention: `D` is moment degree, not linkage-disequilibrium `D`.

hypotheses: ∑ index, weight index * momentSeparationNode D index ^ degree = 0

The diagonal traffic profile through `D` edges generated by a finite

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.IsMomentMatchedProbabilityPair
definitions.body:
(∀ index, momentSeparationNode D index ∈ Set.Icc (1 : ℝ) 2) ∧
    (∀ index, 0 ≤ left index) ∧
    (∀ index, 0 ≤ right index) ∧
    (∑ index, left index = 1) ∧
    (∑ index, right index = 1) ∧
    finiteDiagonalTrafficProfile D left = finiteDiagonalTrafficProfile D right
definitions.docstring:
The complete finite probability-pair contract used by strictness of the
diagonal traffic hierarchy.

Convention: `D` is graph edge depth, not linkage-disequilibrium `D`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.SeparatesAtNextDiagonalTraffic
definitions.body:
finiteDiagonalNextTrafficCoordinate D left ≠
    finiteDiagonalNextTrafficCoordinate D right
definitions.docstring:
The next diagonal coordinate distinguishes a moment-matched pair.

Convention: `D` is graph edge depth, not linkage-disequilibrium `D`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.TrafficInvariantSeparation.IsBlindPairForEveryTruncatedTrafficRisk
definitions.body:
IsMomentMatchedProbabilityPair D left right ∧
    (∀ risk : TruncatedTrafficRisk D,
      risk.evaluate (finiteDiagonalTrafficProfile D left) =
        risk.evaluate (finiteDiagonalTrafficProfile D right)) ∧
    SeparatesAtNextDiagonalTraffic D left right
definitions.docstring:
One pair is simultaneously invisible to every truncated traffic risk and
visible at the next traffic coordinate.

Convention: `D` is graph edge depth, not linkage-disequilibrium `D`.

Per-coordinate quadratic energy of a rank-one positive spike, expressed through the spin's

One distinguished outlier coordinate together with `population` bulk
