definitions.body: ∀ x y, A x y → r x y
definitions.docstring:
**A construction believes an aligner** if every reported alignment is an identification
it makes.  This is the only constraint the data places on a builder.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is a relation between a reported relation and a
chosen equivalence relation; which builders satisfy it is not settled here.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Construction.forcingRel
definitions.docstring:
Three positions, and the two alignments a pairwise aligner reports on them: `0` with `1`,
and `1` with `2`.  It says nothing about `0` and `2`, which is the ordinary situation -- those
two were never compared.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is an explicit finite relation exhibited to
witness that the closure adds pairs; it models no particular alignment.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Construction.support
definitions.signature: {Pos Hap : Type*} (hap : Pos → Hap) (r : Setoid Pos) (x : Pos) : Set Hap
definitions.body: {h | ∃ y, r x y ∧ hap y = h}
definitions.docstring:
**The haplotype support of a node**: which haplotypes are represented in the class of `x`.
A node frequency spectrum is the distribution of the size of this set, so it is the quantity
a core/accessory split is computed from.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It names the image of a class under `hap`; what
the spectrum of a real pangenome looks like is not settled here.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Construction.CollapseFree
definitions.signature: {Pos Hap : Type*} (hap : Pos → Hap) (r : Setoid Pos) : Prop
definitions.body: ∀ x y, r x y → hap x = hap y → x = y
definitions.docstring:
**A construction is collapse-free** when it identifies no two distinct positions of the
same haplotype.  Its failure is a repeat: the same haplotype visiting one node twice.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It names a property of an equivalence relation;
whether the closure of a real alignment set has it is exactly the empirical question about
repeat content, and is not settled here.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Construction.IsCore
definitions.signature: {Pos Hap : Type*} (hap : Pos → Hap) (r : Setoid Pos) (S : Set Hap) (x : Pos) : Prop
definitions.docstring:
**A node is core to a sample** when every haplotype in the sample is represented in it.
This is what "present in every genome examined" means once positions have been quotiented
into nodes, and it is stated against an explicit sample so that the dependence is visible in
the type rather than carried by a convention.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It names a property of a node relative to a set of
haplotypes; which nodes are core in a real panel is not settled here.

which their walks spell different sequences.  One base here, so `0` or `1`.

of the two walks, so it cannot depend on a choice of spanning tree.

different genotypes.  Unlike `seqDist` this *does* take a reference tree.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.piRows6

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.thetaW6
definitions.docstring:
Six times Watterson's `θ_W = S / a_n`, at `n = 3` where `a_3 = 3/2`, so
`6 θ_W = 4 S`.

The factor `4` is `6 / a₃` and is NOT computed here.  `a₃` is a value of the general
harmonic sum, `Descent.Coalescent.harmonicSum 2`, and
`Descent.Pangenome.thetaW6_eq_watterson` proves this definition equals six times
`Descent.Coalescent.wattersonEstimator` at `n = 3`.  The literal is written out rather
than divided because everything in this file must stay in `ℕ` for `decide`; the theorem
is what keeps it from being an assertion.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Gauge.walkDist
definitions.signature: (edges : List E) (w₁ w₂ : Walk E) : Nat
definitions.body: count (fun e ↦ !(w₁ e == w₂ e)) edges
definitions.docstring: Number of edges at which two walks differ.  Walk-level: no tree.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Gauge.rowDist
definitions.signature: (edges : List E) (T : Tree E) (w₁ w₂ : Walk E) : Nat
definitions.body: count (fun e ↦ !(w₁ e == w₂ e) && !T e) edges
definitions.docstring: Number of VCF rows at which two walks carry different genotypes.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Gauge.GaugeInvariant
definitions.signature: {α : Type v} (F : Tree E → List (Walk E) → α) : Prop
definitions.body: ∀ T₁ T₂ : Tree E, ∀ s : List (Walk E), F T₁ s = F T₂ s
definitions.docstring:
A statistic of the catalogue is gauge-invariant when it does not depend on
the reference tree.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Gauge.FactorsThroughWalks
definitions.signature: {α : Type v} (F : Tree E → List (Walk E) → α) : Prop
definitions.body: ∃ f : List (Walk E) → α, ∀ T s, F T s = f s
definitions.docstring:
A catalogue statistic factors through the biological walks when the reference-tree
argument can be removed from its definition.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Gauge.totalWalkDist
definitions.body: sum (fun w₁ ↦ sum (fun w₂ ↦ walkDist edges w₁ w₂) sample) sample
definitions.docstring:
Mean pairwise walk distance, scaled by the number of unordered pairs to stay
in `Nat`.  The sequence-level `π` of `GaugeCounterexample` is this functional
with one base per edge.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Gauge.walkOf
definitions.body: fun e ↦ if h = e then 1 else 0
definitions.docstring: A haplotype as a walk: it traverses its own allele's edge once.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Gauge.treeOf
definitions.docstring: A reference tree as a characteristic function.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Gauge.sampleSub
definitions.docstring: The subsample `[A, A, C]` of `GaugeCounterexample`, as walks.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Gauge.samplePanel
definitions.docstring: The full panel `[A, C, G]`, as walks.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.transitDeficit
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → Fin n) : ℝ
definitions.docstring:
**What the graph's compression costs in tree depth**: the panel's expected time to a
common ancestor, less the graph's.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  Both terms are `Coalescent.meanTransitTime`, K-G (5.7), off the
rate ladder; the only new content is that the second is evaluated at `Linkage.width s`, which
is `Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.Reduction`'s theorem and not an assumption here.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.graphWatterson
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (θ : Descent.Core.Theta) (s : Fin n → Fin n) : ℝ
definitions.docstring:
**What a study reports for `θ`** when it reads its segregating sites off a pangenome
graph and its sample size off the panel that built the graph.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  `Coalescent.expectedSegregatingSites` at the graph's sample size
is `Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.Reduction`'s identification of that sample size;
`Coalescent.wattersonEstimator` at `n` is what the study does.  This file introduces neither
and composes them.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.graphTajimaNumerator
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (θ : Descent.Core.Theta) (s : Fin n → Fin n) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
definitions.body:
Coalescent.expectedPairwiseDifferences θ
    - Coalescent.wattersonEstimator (graphExpectedSegregatingSites θ s) m
definitions.docstring:
**Tajima's numerator as a study computes it from a pangenome graph**: pairwise diversity,
which the graph does not touch, less Watterson's estimator applied to the graph's segregating
sites at a DECLARED sample size `m`.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  Both terms are the corpus's own
(`Coalescent.expectedPairwiseDifferences`, `Coalescent.wattersonEstimator`); the only new
content is that the sites are the graph's, which is
`Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.WidthProfile.graphExpectedSegregatingSites`, and that the
divisor's `m` need not equal the graph's `w`.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.mergerDepth
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → Fin n) : ℕ
definitions.docstring:
**The number of coalescences a pangenome graph performs when it is built.**  The panel
brings `n` lineages and the graph starts with `w`; the difference was coalesced by the
builder rather than by the population.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  It is `Fintype.card` minus `Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.width`,
and `coalescencePath_bot_graphKer` is the theorem that the difference counts coalescences
rather than merely measuring a gap.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.graphPresentation
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → Fin n) : Presentation (Fin n)
definitions.docstring:
**The categorical presentation carried by an interface.**  Empty states of `Fin n` are
removed by restricting to the range, so the result satisfies `Presentation`'s rule that every
coordinate be supported by the panel.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.graphKer
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → Fin n) : Coalescent.ER n
definitions.docstring:
The identity a pangenome graph has already destroyed at interface `s`: two sampled
haplotypes are one object to the graph exactly when they occupy the same graph state.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is `Setoid.ker` of the interface map, read as
a coalescent state; whether a given graph merges a given pair is the empirical question and
is not settled here.

hypotheses: observed s η = observed s η'

Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.eq_of_: observed s η = observed s η'

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.observed
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → Fin n) (ξ : Coalescent.ER n) : Coalescent.ER n
definitions.docstring:
**What a graph at interface `s` reports of the coalescent state `ξ`.**

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  The join is the least equivalence relation above
both arguments; the modelling content is the choice of `graphKer s` as the resolution, which
`Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.Interface` justifies and this file assumes.

hypotheses: observed s η = observed s η'

Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.eq_of_: observed s η = observed s η'

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.GraphState
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → Fin n) (ξ : Coalescent.ER n) : Prop
definitions.docstring:
**A coalescent state a graph at interface `s` can express**: one at or above the merge
the graph was built with.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It names an up-set of `𝓔ₙ`; whether a real
genealogy has passed into it by a given time is the empirical question, and is not settled
here.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.graphMeanTransitTime
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → Fin n) : ℝ
definitions.docstring:
**The pangenome graph coalescent's mean transit time.**  `E(T_w)`, the expected time for
a graph at interface `s` to see its `w` nodes reduced to one, in units where a pair
coalesces at rate `1`.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  It is `Coalescent.meanTransitTime` -- K-G (5.7), off the rate
ladder and nothing else -- evaluated at `Linkage.width s` rather than at the panel size, and
`blocks_le_width_of_graphState` is why that is the right argument.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.ObservablyMarkov
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → Fin n) : Prop
definitions.body:
∀ ξ ξ' : Coalescent.ER n, observed s ξ = observed s ξ' → ∀ v : Coalescent.ER n,
    Nonempty ({η : Coalescent.ER n // Coalescent.Covers ξ η ∧ observed s η = v} ≃
      {η : Coalescent.ER n // Coalescent.Covers ξ' η ∧ observed s η = v})
definitions.docstring:
**Rosenblatt's criterion, K-G (5.1), for a pangenome graph's report.**  Two coalescent
states the graph cannot tell apart must offer equally many transitions into each report, or
the report is not a Markov chain.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is a property of the pair `(s, 𝓔ₙ)` decided by
combinatorics, and `observablyMarkov_of_injective` and `not_observablyMarkov` decide it.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.widthProfile
definitions.docstring:
**The graph coalescent's sample size, locus by locus.**  One entry per interface of the
chain, each the number of graph states occupied there.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  Each entry is `Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.width` of the
corresponding interface, and that this is the sample size rather than a summary of the
topology is `Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.Reduction`.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.graphExpectedSegregatingSites
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (θ : Descent.Core.Theta) (s : Fin n → Fin n) : ℝ
definitions.docstring:
**The diversity a graph reports at one interface**: Watterson's expectation at the
graph's own sample size rather than the panel's.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  It is `Coalescent.expectedSegregatingSites` evaluated at
`Linkage.width s`; the identification of that argument as the sample size is
`Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.Reduction` and is not assumed here.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.graphSingletonShare
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → Fin n) : ℝ
definitions.docstring:
**The share of the graph's reported variation that is singletons**, at one interface.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  `Descent.Coalescent.SiteFrequencySpectrum.singletonShare_eq`
shows the share is `1 / a_{k-1}` for a sample of `k`, with `θ` cancelling;
`graphSingletonShare_eq` is that identity at `k = Linkage.width s`.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.graphSpectrum
definitions.docstring:
**The `i`-th frequency class as a graph reports it.**  The height is the coalescent's own
`E(ξ_i)`, because a graph changes the sample size and not the mutation process; what the
graph changes is which `i` exist, and that is carried by `graphSpectrumClasses` below.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  It is `Coalescent.expectedSpectrum` with no new content; the
content is in the range of `i` it is summed over.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.graphSpectrumClasses
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → Fin n) : ℕ
definitions.docstring:
**How many classes a graph has**: one for each `i = 1, …, w-1`, where `w` is the graph's
width.  This is the whole difference between a graph spectrum and a panel spectrum, and it is
a consequence of `Reduction`'s identification of the entrance point rather than a new
assumption.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  `Linkage.width s` is the graph's node count, which
`GraphCoalescent.blocks_graphKer` identifies with the coalescent's block count.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.graphSpectrumMissing
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (θ : Descent.Core.Theta) (s : Fin n → Fin n) : ℝ
definitions.body: expectedSegregatingSites θ n - expectedSegregatingSites θ (Linkage.width s)
definitions.docstring:
**The spectrum mass a graph does not report**: the panel's total less the graph's.

The classes `i = w, …, n-1` have no counterpart in a graph of width `w`, and they are the
HIGH-frequency classes.  That is forced by what merging does: two haplotypes merged into one
node cannot disagree at any site, so the variants a graph destroys are exactly the ones many
haplotypes shared.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  Both terms are `Coalescent.expectedSegregatingSites`.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.graphVarTransitTime
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → Fin n) : ℝ
definitions.docstring:
**The spread the graph coalescent reports**: the panel's formula at the graph's own
entrance point.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  It is `Coalescent.varTransitTime` at `Linkage.width s`, which is
`Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.Reduction`'s identification of the sample size and not a
new assumption.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GraphCoalescent.graphVarianceDeficit
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → Fin n) : ℝ
definitions.docstring:
**The spread a graph does not report**: the panel's variance less the graph's.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  Both terms are `Coalescent.varTransitTime`.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GromovWeak.polynomial
definitions.signature: {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] (k : ℕ) (r : ι → ι → ℝ) (f : (Fin k → Fin k → ℝ) → ℝ) : ℝ
definitions.body: ((Fintype.card ι : ℝ) ^ k)⁻¹ * ∑ x : Fin k → ι, f (fun i j ↦ r (x i) (x j))
definitions.docstring:
**The degree-`k` polynomial of a sample's distance with test function `f`**: draw `k`
sample members uniformly and independently, form their distance matrix, and average `f` of
it.  This is the generating family for the Gromov-weak topology, at a uniform measure on a
finite sample.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is an average over a finite index type; what
carries empirical weight is the reading of `r` as a genealogical or sequence distance, and
that reading is supplied by whoever instantiates it.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GromovWeak.pairwiseDiversity
definitions.signature: {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] (r : ι → ι → ℝ) : ℝ
definitions.docstring:
**Pairwise diversity is the degree-two polynomial.**  `π` is what you get by drawing two
sample members and averaging their distance, which is the smallest nonconstant member of the
family.  That it sits inside the invariant family is the structural reason it survives the
reference-tree gauge, where `S` does not.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GromovWeak.FactorsThroughDistance
definitions.signature: {ι : Type u} {X : Type*} (dist : X → ι → ι → ℝ) (stat : X → ℝ) : Prop
definitions.body: ∃ Φ : (ι → ι → ℝ) → ℝ, ∀ x, stat x = Φ (dist x)
definitions.docstring:
**A statistic factors through the sample's distance.**  `dist x` is the distance matrix
that construction `x` presents and `stat x` the number reported from it; factoring says the
number was a function of the matrix all along.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is a property of a pair of functions, decided
by `factorsThroughDistance_polynomial` on one side and `not_factorsThroughDistance` on the
other.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.GromovWeak.treeDistance
definitions.docstring:
The distances a pangenome sample carries, presented as a function of the reference tree.
It ignores its argument, which is the whole point: sequence distance is a property of the
walks, and the tree is a choice made after the walks exist.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Growth.expectedPanSize
definitions.docstring:
**The expected pan size**: the size law `PanelGraph.nodeCount_eq_add_segregatingCount`
taken in expectation under the neutral coalescent.  A reference of `base` nodes plus the
expected segregating-locus count of a panel of `mSample` haplotypes.

Empirical status: MIXED, inherited from `Coalescent.expectedSegregatingSites` -- the tree
factor is derived, the Poisson-mutation and infinite-sites premises are assumed, and the
verdicts are recorded there.  `base` is a modelling input, not a derived quantity.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HaplotypeGluing.TwoChartPanel.chart
definitions.signature: (P : TwoChartPanel Global Left Right Overlap) (h : Global) : Left × Right
definitions.docstring: The pair of local sections carried by an observed global haplotype.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HaplotypeGluing.TwoChartPanel.Compatible
definitions.signature: (P : TwoChartPanel Global Left Right Overlap) (z : Left × Right) : Prop
definitions.docstring: A left/right pair satisfies the matching condition on the overlap.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HaplotypeGluing.TwoChartPanel.observedSections
definitions.signature: (P : TwoChartPanel Global Left Right Overlap) : Set (Left × Right)
definitions.docstring: Global chromosomes actually observed in the panel, represented in the two charts.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HaplotypeGluing.TwoChartPanel.matchingClosure
definitions.signature: (P : TwoChartPanel Global Left Right Overlap) : Set (Left × Right)
definitions.body: {z | P.Compatible z ∧ z.1 ∈ Set.range P.left ∧ z.2 ∈ Set.range P.right}
definitions.docstring:
Compatible local pieces observed somewhere in the left and right marginals.  The donors
of the two pieces need not be the same global chromosome.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HaplotypeGluing.TwoChartPanel.splice
definitions.docstring: Cross the left piece of `a` with the right piece of `b`.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HaplotypeGluing.TwoChartPanel.RecombinationClosed
definitions.signature: (P : TwoChartPanel Global Left Right Overlap) (T : Set (Left × Right)) : Prop
definitions.body: ∀ a ∈ T, ∀ b ∈ T, P.Compatible (splice a b) → splice a b ∈ T
definitions.docstring:
A collection is closed under every crossover whose two chosen pieces match on the
overlap.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  A closure condition on a set of local sections;
it names no observable and carries no free parameter.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HaplotypeGluing.TwoChartPanel.gluingDefect
definitions.signature: (P : TwoChartPanel Global Left Right Overlap) : Set (Left × Right)
definitions.docstring: Locally observed, overlap-compatible haplotypes absent from the observed global panel.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HaplotypeGluing.TwoChartPanel.HasGluing
definitions.signature: (P : TwoChartPanel Global Left Right Overlap) : Prop
definitions.docstring:
The observed haplotypes satisfy effective two-chart gluing when every locally observed,
overlap-compatible matching family is already globally observed.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HaplotypeGluing.TwoChartPanel.interfacePanel
definitions.signature: (s : ι → ι) : TwoChartPanel ι ι ι ι where left
definitions.ret_type: TwoChartPanel ι ι ι ι where left
definitions.body:
id
  right := id
  leftOverlap := s
  rightOverlap := s
  compatible := fun _ ↦ rfl
definitions.docstring:
The two charts on either side of one graph interface.  A donor is visible as itself in
each module and only its interface state is visible on the overlap.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HaplotypeGluing.probabilisticGluingResidual
definitions.docstring:
Probability mass of a global section minus the mass predicted by independent gluing of
its left and right marginals.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HaplotypeGluing.binaryGluingResidual
definitions.docstring: The gluing residual for the `11` cell of a binary two-locus table.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HaplotypeGluing.binaryLinkageDeterminant
definitions.docstring:
The classical determinant form of two-locus linkage disequilibrium.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  An algebraic combination of the table's own four cells, with no
free parameter; `binaryGluingResidual_eq_tableDeterminant` derives it from the gluing
residual under normalization alone.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HomologyGroupoid.coarseSetoid
definitions.signature: (C : Type u) [Groupoid.{v} C] : Setoid C where r x y
definitions.ret_type: Setoid C where r x y
definitions.body:
Nonempty (x ⟶ y)
  iseqv := by
    refine ⟨fun x ↦ ⟨𝟙 x⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rintro x y ⟨f⟩
      exact ⟨Groupoid.inv f⟩
    · rintro x y z ⟨f⟩ ⟨g⟩
      exact ⟨f ≫ g⟩
definitions.docstring:
Propositional truncation of a groupoid.  It remembers that a witness exists and forgets
which witness, how many witnesses, and the isotropy action on them.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HomologyGroupoid.coarsePresentation
definitions.docstring: The ordinary pangenome presentation obtained by forgetting homology witnesses.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HomologyGroupoid.coarsePresentationOfCharts
definitions.signature: {I : Type u} (P : ChartGroupoidRelation I) : Presentation P.Obj
definitions.docstring:
The coarse presentation of the exact chart groupoid.  This is the single bridge from the
finite atlas core to the representation-invariant semantic quotient.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.meanLog
definitions.body: (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ h : ι, Real.log (v h)
definitions.docstring:
The mean logarithm of a positive vector on the panel: the logarithm of its geometric
mean.  This is the quantity the chain carries.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.linkagePressure
definitions.docstring: **Linkage-entropy pressure**: the identity a chain of separators forgets, summed.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.witnessLeft
definitions.body: fun h ↦ if h = 2 then 2 else 0
definitions.docstring: The interface separating `{0,1}` from `{2}`.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.witnessRight
definitions.body: fun h ↦ if h = 1 then 1 else 0
definitions.docstring: The interface separating `{0,2}` from `{1}`, which cuts the panel the other way.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.diagonals
definitions.docstring: The `m` panel threads, as the derivations that never switch donor.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.phantoms
definitions.docstring: **The panel-phantom derivations**: compatible mosaics the panel does not contain.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.Chain
definitions.docstring: An ordered interface chain: one state map per separator, in crossing order.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.mosaicsFrom
definitions.body:
| [], h => {[h]}
  | s :: c, h => (fiber s h).biUnion fun g ↦ (mosaicsFrom c g).image (h :: ·)
definitions.docstring:
The ancestry-resolved derivations over `c` whose first module is supplied by donor `h`.
A derivation over a chain of `r` interfaces is a list of `r + 1` donors, and switching is
permitted only between donors sharing a state at the interface they meet at.

equations.rhs: (fiber s h).biUnion fun g ↦ (mosaicsFrom c g).image (h :: ·)

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.mosaics
definitions.docstring: Every ancestry-resolved derivation over the chain `c`.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.derivationCount
definitions.body:
| [], _ => 1
  | s :: c, h => ∑ g ∈ fiber s h, derivationCount c g
definitions.docstring:
The number of legal continuations of a prefix ending at donor `h`: the chain form of the
tree dynamic program.  Each interface costs one pass over the panel, so the whole count is
`O(m·r)` arithmetic operations and never enumerates a path.

equations.rhs: ∑ g ∈ fiber s h, derivationCount c g

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.switches
definitions.body:
| [] => 0
  | [_] => 0
  | a :: b :: t => (if a = b then 0 else 1) + switches (b :: t)
definitions.docstring: The number of interfaces at which a derivation changes donor.

equations.rhs: (if a = b then 0 else 1) + switches (b :: t)

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.switchPolynomial
definitions.body:
| [], _, _ => 1
  | s :: c, h, z => ∑ g ∈ fiber s h, (if h = g then 1 else z) * switchPolynomial c g z
definitions.docstring:
The switch-graded derivation count: the dynamic program with a weight `z` charged at
every donor change.

equations.rhs: ∑ g ∈ fiber s h, (if h = g then 1 else z) * switchPolynomial c g z

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.stateMass
definitions.signature: (p : ι → ℝ) (s : ι → ι) (h : ι) : ℝ
definitions.body: ∑ g ∈ fiber s h, p g
definitions.docstring: The mass the law `p` puts on the graph state that `h` occupies.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.condIdentityLoss
definitions.body: ∑ h : ι, p h * Real.log (stateMass p s h / p h)
definitions.docstring: `H_p(J ∣ S)`: the thread identity an interface forgets, weighing threads by `p`.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.panelEntropy
definitions.body: ∑ h : ι, p h * Real.log (1 / p h)
definitions.docstring: `H(p)`, the identity the panel carries before any interface has merged anything.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.freePotential
definitions.body: ∑ h : ι, p h * Real.log (v h / p h)
definitions.docstring: The potential the chain carries: `∑ p log (v/p)`.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.condLinkagePressure
definitions.docstring: Linkage-entropy pressure under the law `p`.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.stateEntropy
definitions.body:
∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.image s,
    (∑ g ∈ stateFiber s a, p g) * Real.log (1 / ∑ g ∈ stateFiber s a, p g)
definitions.docstring: `H(S)`: the entropy of the graph state a `p`-random thread occupies.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.stateFiber
definitions.body: Finset.univ.filter fun g ↦ s g = a
definitions.docstring: The threads whose graph state at interface `s` is `a`.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.fiber
definitions.docstring: The threads that interface `s` cannot tell apart from `h`.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.fiberCard
definitions.docstring: How many panel threads share `h`'s graph state at interface `s`.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.width
definitions.docstring:
The number of OCCUPIED graph states at interface `s`.  States no thread reaches are
invisible to every statement here, which is what makes this the right `w`.

hypotheses: ∀ g h : ι, s g = s h → ρ g = ρ h → g = h

Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.card_le_width_: ∀ g h : ι, s g = s h → ρ g = ρ h → g = h
Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.width_eq_card_: ∀ g h : ι, s g = s h → ρ g = ρ h → g = h
Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.card_aux_ge_of: ∀ g h : ι, s g = s h → ρ g = ρ h → g = h

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.identityLoss
definitions.body: (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ h : ι, Real.log (fiberCard s h : ℝ)
definitions.docstring:
**The identity a single interface forgets**, in nats.

For a thread `J` drawn uniformly from the panel and `S = s J` its graph state, this is
exactly the conditional entropy `H(J ∣ S)`: the residual uncertainty about which haplotype
arrived, once the topology has said only which state it is in.  Written as a mean over
threads rather than over states, so that `sum_fiberwise` moves it either way.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.stateFreq
definitions.docstring: The fraction of the panel occupying graph state `a`: the vector `q` of the width law.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.imbalance
definitions.body: ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.image s, stateFreq s a * Real.log (stateFreq s a * (width s : ℝ))
definitions.docstring:
**The imbalance tax**: the Kullback–Leibler divergence, in nats, of the state-frequency
vector from the uniform law on the occupied states.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.Resolves
definitions.signature: (s : ι → ι) (aux : ι → A) (ρ : ι → R) : Prop
definitions.body: ∀ g h : ι, s g = s h → aux g = aux h → ρ g = ρ h
definitions.docstring:
A controller with auxiliary state `aux` RESOLVES the residual class `ρ` at interface `s`
when the graph state and the auxiliary state together determine it.  `ρ h` is whatever the
legal continuations after arriving on thread `h` depend on; when the panel's suffixes
identify their thread, `ρ` is injective and resolving it means recovering the donor.

hypotheses: ∀ g ∈ t, ∀ h ∈ t, ρ g = ρ h → g = h
∀ g h : ι, s g = s h → ρ g = ρ h → g = h

Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.card_le_card_a: ∀ g ∈ t, ∀ h ∈ t, ρ g = ρ h → g = h
Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.card_le_width_: ∀ g h : ι, s g = s h → ρ g = ρ h → g = h
Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.width_eq_card_: ∀ g h : ι, s g = s h → ρ g = ρ h → g = h
Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.card_aux_ge_of: ∀ g h : ι, s g = s h → ρ g = ρ h → g = h

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.spell
definitions.signature: (code : ι → List α) (x : List ι) : List α
definitions.docstring: The word a derivation spells: each module contributes its donor's block.

hypotheses: ∀ b : List α, (Finset.univ.filter fun g ↦ code g = b

Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.sum_ite_spell_: ∀ b : List α, (Finset.univ.filter fun g ↦ code g = b
Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.card_filter_sp: ∀ b : List α, (Finset.univ.filter fun g ↦ code g = b

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.PrefixFree
definitions.body: ∀ g h : ι, g ≠ h → ¬ code g <+: code h
definitions.docstring: A block system is PREFIX-FREE when no donor's block begins another donor's block.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.spelledWords
definitions.signature: (code : ι → List α) (c : Chain ι) : Finset (List α)
definitions.docstring: The distinct words the compatible language spells.

hypotheses: ∀ b : List α, (Finset.univ.filter fun g ↦ code g = b

Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.card_mosaics_l: ∀ b : List α, (Finset.univ.filter fun g ↦ code g = b

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.panelWords
definitions.signature: (code : ι → List α) (c : Chain ι) : Finset (List α)
definitions.docstring: The words the panel itself spells.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.phantomWords
definitions.signature: (code : ι → List α) (c : Chain ι) : Finset (List α)
definitions.body: spelledWords code c \ panelWords code c
definitions.docstring: The words the topology spells that the panel does not contain.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.snpCode
definitions.body: (Finset.univ : Finset ι).toList.map fun g ↦ if g = h then Allele.C else Allele.A
definitions.docstring:
The block donor `h` contributes: the all-`A` reference word carrying a single `C` at
`h`'s own coordinate.  One biallelic SNP per block, and nothing else.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.combCode
definitions.docstring:
A block system of VARIABLE length: donor `i` contributes `A^i C`.  This is the unary comb
code, the smallest witness that prefix-freeness is strictly weaker than fixed length — the
blocks have `i + 1` distinct lengths, so no fixed-length hypothesis reaches them, and
`combCode_prefixFree` shows the decodability results here do.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.spliceWalk
definitions.signature: (seg : ι → Gauge.Walk E) (x : List ι) : Gauge.Walk E
definitions.body: fun e ↦ (x.map fun h ↦ seg h e).sum
definitions.docstring:
The walk a derivation traverses: each module contributes its donor's segment, and
traversal counts add.  This is the walk-level datum of `Descent.Pangenome.Gauge`, which
mentions no reference tree.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.Arbor.size
definitions.body:
| Arbor.nil => 0
  | Arbor.child _ t rest => 1 + t.size + rest.size
definitions.docstring: The number of edges, equivalently the number of modules other than the root.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.arborWidthProd
definitions.body:
| Arbor.nil => 1
  | Arbor.child s t rest => width s * arborWidthProd t * arborWidthProd rest
definitions.docstring: The product of the occupied widths over every edge of the tree.

equations.rhs: width s * arborWidthProd t * arborWidthProd rest

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.arborCount
definitions.body:
| Arbor.nil, _ => 1
  | Arbor.child s t rest, h => (∑ g ∈ fiber s h, arborCount t g) * arborCount rest h
definitions.docstring: The number of ways to complete the subtree below a module supplied by donor `h`.

equations.rhs: (∑ g ∈ fiber s h, arborCount t g) * arborCount rest h

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.arborMosaicsFrom
definitions.docstring:
The derivations completing the subtree below a module supplied by `h`, serialised in
first-child order.  The donor of the module itself is NOT in the list; it is the `h` the
list is indexed by, and the top-level `arborMosaics` puts it back.

equations.rhs: (fiber s h).biUnion fun g ↦ ((arborMosaicsFrom t g) ×ˢ (arborMosaicsFrom rest h)).image fun p ↦ g :: (p.1 ++ p.2)

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.arborMosaics
definitions.docstring: Every derivation over the tree, with the root module's donor at the head.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.arborPressure
definitions.body:
| Arbor.nil => 0
  | Arbor.child s t rest => identityLoss s + arborPressure t + arborPressure rest
definitions.docstring: **Linkage-entropy pressure over a tree**: the identity every edge forgets, summed.

equations.rhs: identityLoss s + arborPressure t + arborPressure rest

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Linkage.chainArbor
definitions.body:
| [] => Arbor.nil
  | s :: c => Arbor.child s (chainArbor c) Arbor.nil
definitions.docstring: A chain, as a tree in which every module has exactly one child.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.PanelGraph.posAlign
definitions.signature: {m n : ℕ} (H : Fin m → Core.Haplotype n) : Fin m × Core.Locus n → Fin m × Core.Locus n → Prop
definitions.ret_type: Fin m × Core.Locus n → Fin m × Core.Locus n → Prop
definitions.body: fun p q ↦ p.2 = q.2 ∧ H p.1 p.2 = H q.1 q.2
definitions.docstring:
**Positional homology**: two panel positions are aligned when they sit at the same
locus and carry the same allele.  This is the relation a reference-coordinate pipeline
asserts -- every haplotype is indexed by the same `Core.Locus`, so every pair of positions
is compared, through the coordinate system rather than through a pairwise aligner.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It names a relation induced by a panel; whether
positional homology is the homology a study wants at a structurally variable locus is the
empirical question, and is not settled here.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.PanelGraph.posSetoid
definitions.signature: {m n : ℕ} (H : Fin m → Core.Haplotype n) : Setoid (Fin m × Core.Locus n)
definitions.docstring:
**The positional construction**: the setoid positional homology already is.  No closure
is taken because none is needed, which is the point recorded by `closure_posAlign`.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It packages `posAlign` with its equivalence
proof; nothing about a population is asserted.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.PanelGraph.posPresentation
definitions.signature: {m n : ℕ} (H : Fin m → Core.Haplotype n) : Presentation (Fin m × Core.Locus n)
definitions.docstring:
**The positional graph as an object of the presentation category.**  Its coordinate
carrier is the quotient by locus-and-allele identity, and the quotient map embeds every
observed panel position into that carrier.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.PanelGraph.closurePresentationIso
definitions.signature: {m n : ℕ} (H : Fin m → Core.Haplotype n) : Presentation.closurePresentation (posAlign H) ≅ posPresentation H
definitions.body:
by
  apply Presentation.isoOfKernelEq
  simpa [Presentation.closurePresentation, posPresentation] using closure_posAlign H
definitions.docstring:
**The positional graph is the universal presentation of its alignments.**  The earlier
setoid equality becomes an isomorphism in the presentation category, making precise that a
different coordinate carrier with the same positional homology is not a different graph
object.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.PanelGraph.SegregatesAt
definitions.signature: {m n : ℕ} (H : Fin m → Core.Haplotype n) (l : Core.Locus n) : Prop
definitions.body: ∃ i j : Fin m, H i l ≠ H j l
definitions.docstring:
**A locus segregates** when two panel haplotypes disagree there.  This is the panel's
own Watterson `S`, locus by locus, before any model is put on the panel.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It names a property of a given panel at a given
locus; which loci of a real panel segregate is data, not derivation.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.PanelGraph.nodesAt
definitions.signature: {m n : ℕ} (H : Fin m → Core.Haplotype n) (l : Core.Locus n) : Finset Core.Allele
definitions.body: Finset.image (fun i ↦ H i l) Finset.univ
definitions.docstring:
**The nodes at a locus**: the alleles the panel presents there.  A positional graph
has one node per allele per locus, and this is that column of it.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  A finite image; what a real panel presents is
data.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.PanelGraph.nodeCount
definitions.signature: {m n : ℕ} (H : Fin m → Core.Haplotype n) : ℕ
definitions.docstring:
**The size of the graph**: nodes summed over loci.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  A count of a given panel's graph; the pan-size
a study reports for a real panel is data, and `nodeCount_eq_add_segregatingCount` is what
that number is made of.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.PanelGraph.segregatingCount
definitions.signature: {m n : ℕ} (H : Fin m → Core.Haplotype n) : ℕ
definitions.docstring:
**The panel's segregating-locus count** -- Watterson's `S`, computed from a concrete
panel rather than posited as a summary.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  A count of a given panel.  What connects it to
the coalescent's `E(S)` is a model, and the connection is made in
`Descent.Pangenome.Growth`, not here.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.Hom.id
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} (P : Presentation Pos) : Hom P P where toFun
definitions.body:
fun x ↦ x
  comm := fun _ ↦ rfl
definitions.docstring: Identity map of a presentation.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.Hom.comp
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} {P Q R : Presentation Pos} (f : Hom P Q) (g : Hom Q R) : Hom P R where toFun
definitions.body:
g.toFun ∘ f.toFun
  comm := fun x ↦ by rw [Function.comp_apply, f.comm, g.comm]
definitions.docstring: Composition of commuting coordinate maps.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.kernel
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} (P : Presentation Pos) : Setoid Pos
definitions.docstring: The relation on panel positions represented by a presentation.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.homOfKernelLE
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} {P Q : Presentation Pos} (h : P.kernel ≤ Q.kernel) : P ⟶ Q where toFun y
definitions.body:
Q.encode (Classical.choose (P.onto y))
  comm := fun x ↦ by
    let hx := Classical.choose_spec (P.onto (P.encode x))
    apply h at hx
    exact hx
definitions.docstring:
A containment of kernel relations induces the unique commuting coordinate map.

The definition chooses one panel position above each source coordinate.  Kernel containment
makes the target coordinate independent of that choice.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.ofMap
definitions.signature: {Pos Coord : Type u} (f : Pos → Coord) : Presentation Pos where Coord
definitions.body:
Set.range f
  encode x := ⟨f x, x, rfl⟩
  onto y := by
    obtain ⟨_, x, rfl⟩ := y
    exact ⟨x, rfl⟩
definitions.docstring:
Any map from panel positions becomes a presentation after restricting its codomain to
the coordinates it actually uses.  The restriction removes dead graph states.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.ofSetoid
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} (r : Setoid Pos) : Presentation Pos where Coord
definitions.body:
Quotient r
  encode := Quotient.mk r
  onto q := Quotient.inductionOn q fun x ↦ ⟨x, rfl⟩
definitions.docstring: Every setoid gives a canonical presentation by its quotient map.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.isoOfKernelEq
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} {P Q : Presentation Pos} (h : P.kernel = Q.kernel) : P ≅ Q where hom
definitions.docstring:
Equal kernel relations construct an isomorphism of presentations.  The inverse laws need
no coordinate calculation: thinness makes every pair of parallel arrows equal.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.coordEquivOfIso
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} {P Q : Presentation Pos} (i : P ≅ Q) : P.Coord ≃ Q.Coord where toFun
definitions.body:
i.hom.toFun
  invFun := i.inv.toFun
  left_inv y := by
    have h := congrArg Hom.toFun i.hom_inv_id
    exact congrFun h y
  right_inv y := by
    have h := congrArg Hom.toFun i.inv_hom_id
    exact congrFun h y
definitions.docstring:
An isomorphism of presentations induces an equivalence of their coordinate carriers.
This is stated explicitly because `Presentation` is not made a concrete category merely to
obtain the carrier map.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.canonicalIso
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} (P : Presentation Pos) : P ≅ ofSetoid P.kernel
definitions.docstring:
Every presentation is isomorphic to the canonical quotient by its kernel.  This is the
normal form behind the classification theorem.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.reindex
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} (P : Presentation Pos) {Coord : Type u} (e : P.Coord ≃ Coord) : Presentation Pos where Coord
definitions.body:
Coord
  encode := e ∘ P.encode
  onto := e.surjective.comp P.onto
definitions.docstring: Relabel a presentation's coordinates through a bijection.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.reindexIso
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} (P : Presentation Pos) {Coord : Type u} (e : P.Coord ≃ Coord) : P ≅ reindex P e
definitions.docstring:
**A relabelled coordinate carrier is the same pangenome presentation.**  This covers
identifier permutations, canonical renumberings and orientation conventions whenever they
act bijectively on the represented coordinates.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.IsInvariant
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} {Value : Type v} (F : Presentation Pos → Value) : Prop
definitions.body: ∀ P Q, Nonempty (P ≅ Q) → F P = F Q
definitions.docstring:
A statistic is **representation-invariant** when isomorphic presentations give the same
answer.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.FactorsThroughKernel
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} {Value : Type v} (F : Presentation Pos → Value) : Prop
definitions.body: ∃ f : Setoid Pos → Value, ∀ P, F P = f P.kernel
definitions.docstring:
A statistic **factors through represented homology** when it is a function of the kernel
setoid alone.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.coordinateCount
definitions.docstring:
The number of occupied SEMANTIC coordinates in a presentation.  `Nat.card` makes the
definition independent of a chosen enumeration.  This is deliberately not the number of
storage nodes in one graph serialization; `graphNodeCount_not_invariant` below separates the
two quantities.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.discretePresentation
definitions.signature: (Pos : Type u) : Presentation Pos where Coord
definitions.docstring: The discrete presentation, in which every panel position is its own semantic coordinate.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.atomicGraph
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} (P : Presentation Pos) : GraphPresentation Pos where semantic
definitions.body:
P
  Node := P.Coord
  block := id
  block_onto := surjective_id
definitions.docstring: The atomic storage of a semantic presentation: one node per semantic coordinate.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.GraphEquivalent
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} (G H : GraphPresentation Pos) : Prop
definitions.docstring:
**Lossless graph-presentation equivalence.**  Storage nodes may be split, merged or
renamed; the semantic presentations must remain isomorphic.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.graphSetoid
definitions.signature: (Pos : Type u) : Setoid (GraphPresentation Pos) where r
definitions.docstring: Presentation equivalence as a setoid on storage graphs.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.PangenomeObject
definitions.docstring:
**A pangenome object is an equivalence class of graph presentations.**  Node identifiers,
segmentations and semantic carrier names have been quotiented out.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.classOf
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} (G : GraphPresentation Pos) : PangenomeObject Pos
definitions.docstring: The presentation-equivalence class represented by a storage graph.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.IsGraphInvariant
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} {Value : Type v} (F : GraphPresentation Pos → Value) : Prop
definitions.body: ∀ G H, GraphEquivalent G H → F G = F H
definitions.docstring:
A statistic of storage graphs is invariant when it is constant under lossless graph
presentation equivalence.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.FactorsThroughSemantic
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} {Value : Type v} (F : GraphPresentation Pos → Value) : Prop
definitions.body: ∃ f : Presentation Pos → Value, IsInvariant f ∧ ∀ G, F G = f G.semantic
definitions.docstring:
A storage-graph statistic factors through semantic content when it comes from an
isomorphism-invariant statistic of semantic presentations.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.graphNodeCount
definitions.docstring: The raw number of occupied storage nodes.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.splitNodeWitness
definitions.docstring: Two atomic nodes over the discrete two-position semantic pangenome.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.mergedNodeWitness
definitions.body:
discretePresentation (Fin 2)
  Node := Unit
  block := fun _ ↦ ()
  block_onto := fun y ↦ by
    cases y
    exact ⟨(discretePresentation (Fin 2)).encode 0, rfl⟩
definitions.docstring: One merged node over exactly the same discrete two-position semantic pangenome.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.closurePresentation
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} (A : Pos → Pos → Prop) : Presentation Pos
definitions.docstring: The canonical presentation generated by an alignment relation.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Presentation.Coequalizes
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type u} (A : Pos → Pos → Prop) (P : Presentation Pos) : Prop
definitions.docstring:
A presentation coequalises an alignment relation when every reported aligned pair is
assigned one coordinate.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Register.orbitSum
definitions.signature: (G : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype G] {X : Type*} [MulAction G X] (f : X → ℝ) (x : X) : ℝ
definitions.docstring:
**The orbit sum of a statistic at a point**: the total of `f` over the orbit of `x`,
counted with multiplicity in the group.  Summing rather than averaging keeps the definition
free of a division and so free of a nonvanishing side condition.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is an average of a given function over a given
group action; which group acts on a real pangenome is not settled here.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Register.orbitAverage
definitions.signature: (G : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype G] {X : Type*} [MulAction G X] (f : X → ℝ) (x : X) : ℝ
definitions.body: orbitSum G f x / (Fintype.card G : ℝ)
definitions.docstring: **The orbit average**: the orbit sum divided by the order of the group.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Register.shift
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (k : ZMod n) (a : ZMod n → ℝ) : ZMod n → ℝ
definitions.docstring:
**A change of register on a repeat array of `n` copies.**  The copies are indexed by
`ZMod n` because the array carries a free transitive cyclic action and nothing distinguishes
a starting point; `shift k` is the relabelling that starts counting `k` copies later.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is a reindexing of a function on `ZMod n`.

hypotheses: ∀ D D' : GxEDeployment n, (∀ i, D.shift i = D'.shift i

Descent.PopGen.no_threshold_metric_separ: ∀ D D' : GxEDeployment n, (∀ i, D.shift i = D'.shift i

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Register.registerPresentation
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (k : ZMod n) : Presentation (ZMod n) where Coord
definitions.body:
ZMod n
  encode i := i + k
  onto := (Equiv.addRight k).surjective
definitions.docstring:
**A cyclic register as a pangenome presentation.**  Position `i` receives coordinate
`i + k`, so changing `k` changes only which copy is called first.  Addition by `k` is
surjective, hence no coordinate is dead.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Register.registerPresentationIso
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (k l : ZMod n) : registerPresentation k ≅ registerPresentation l
definitions.docstring:
**Every choice of first repeat copy is the same presentation.**  The existing group
action and the categorical notion of presentation equivalence therefore agree on the cyclic
register example.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Register.RegisterInvariant
definitions.body: ∀ (k : ZMod n) (a : ZMod n → ℝ), F (shift k a) = F a
definitions.docstring:
**A summary of a repeat array is register-invariant** when no change of register moves
it.  Only such summaries are functions of the array; the rest are functions of the labelling.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It names a property of a summary functional;
`shiftInvariant_sum` witnesses that the property is satisfiable.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Strand.doubled
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type*} (S : Pos → Pos → Bool → Prop) : (Pos × Bool) → (Pos × Bool) → Prop
definitions.body: fun a b ↦ ∃ s, S a.1 b.1 s ∧ b.2 = xor a.2 s
definitions.docstring:
**The identification a signed alignment set makes on oriented positions.**

`S p q s` reads "`p` aligns to `q`, inverted iff `s`".  The alignment identifies position `p`
read in direction `b` with position `q` read in direction `b `xor` s`, which is the whole
content of recording an orientation.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It transports a reported relation to `Pos × Bool`;
which alignments a real aligner reports is not settled here.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Strand.strandPresentation
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type*} (S : Pos → Pos → Bool → Prop) : Presentation (Pos × Bool)
definitions.docstring:
**The presentation generated by oriented alignments.**  Its positions are doubled by
strand, and its coordinates are the equivalence classes forced by the oriented alignment
relation.  This places the strand obstruction inside the same presentation category as the
unoriented pangenome construction.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Strand.Frustrated
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type*} (S : Pos → Pos → Bool → Prop) : Prop
definitions.body: ∃ p : Pos, EqvGen (doubled S) (p, false) (p, true)
definitions.docstring:
**A frustrated alignment set** is one whose identifications force some position into a
class with its own reverse complement.  Equivalently: some closed chain of alignments has an
odd number of inversions, so its holonomy is the flip.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It names a property of a reported relation;
`frustratedTriangle_frustrated` witnesses that the property is satisfiable, and whether a
given locus has it is empirical and not settled here.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Strand.GaugeFixing
definitions.signature: {Pos : Type*} (S : Pos → Pos → Bool → Prop) (g : Pos → Bool) : Prop
definitions.body: ∀ p q s, S p q s → g q = xor (g p) s
definitions.docstring:
**A gauge fixing** is a global choice of reading direction consistent with every
alignment at once: one bit per position whose difference across an alignment is exactly that
alignment's inversion bit.  This is what a linear reference coordinate provides, restricted
to what it says about strand.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It names a compatibility between a reported
relation and an assignment; `gaugeFixing_const_of_no_inversion` witnesses that the property
is satisfiable.

hypotheses: ∀ p q s, S p q s → s = false

Descent.Pangenome.Strand.gaugeFixing_con: ∀ p q s, S p q s → s = false

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.Strand.frustratedTriangle
definitions.body:
fun p q s ↦
  (p = 0 ∧ q = 1 ∧ s = false) ∨ (p = 1 ∧ q = 0 ∧ s = false) ∨
  (p = 1 ∧ q = 2 ∧ s = false) ∨ (p = 2 ∧ q = 1 ∧ s = false) ∨
  (p = 2 ∧ q = 0 ∧ s = true) ∨ (p = 0 ∧ q = 2 ∧ s = true)
definitions.docstring:
Three positions and three alignments: `0` to `1` direct, `1` to `2` direct, and `2` back
to `0` INVERTED.  Every alignment is individually unremarkable and the inconsistency exists
only around the cycle.  This is an inversion polymorphism in the smallest form that has one.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is an explicit finite relation exhibited to
witness that frustration occurs; it models no particular locus.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.ChartSymmetry
definitions.docstring: Global structural symmetries of the exact groupoid presented by a chart system.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.ChartIsotropy
definitions.docstring: Local structural symmetry at one object of the exact chart groupoid.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.chartSymmetryEquivWreath
definitions.signature: {I : Type u} (P : ChartGroupoidRelation I) (X : P.Obj) (transport : ∀ Y : P.Obj, X ⟶ Y) : ChartSymmetry P ≃* Descent.Core.Wreath (ChartIsotropy P X) P.Obj
definitions.ret_type: ChartSymmetry P ≃* Descent.Core.Wreath (ChartIsotropy P X) P.Obj
definitions.docstring:
**Local wreath decomposition for pangenome charts.**  Chosen homology transports from
`X` to every chart object identify global structural symmetries with independent local
isotropy states together with permutations of the equivalent objects.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HaplotypeGluing.tripleGluingResidual
definitions.signature: (triple pairAB pairAC pairBC singleA singleB singleC : ℝ) : ℝ
definitions.body:
triple - singleA * pairBC - singleB * pairAC - singleC * pairAB
    + 2 * (singleA * singleB * singleC)
definitions.docstring:
**The third-order gluing residual, in closed form.** The joint mass of three loci, less
each way of gluing it from one pair and the remaining singleton, plus twice the
all-singleton product.

definitions.name: Descent.Pangenome.HaplotypeGluing.bennettThreeLocus
definitions.signature: (triple pairAB pairAC pairBC singleA singleB singleC : ℝ) : ℝ
definitions.body:
triple - singleA * probabilisticGluingResidual pairBC singleB singleC
    - singleB * probabilisticGluingResidual pairAC singleA singleC
    - singleC * probabilisticGluingResidual pairAB singleA singleB
    - singleA * singleB * singleC
definitions.docstring:
**The third-order residual in recursive form.** Each singleton times the PAIRWISE
residual of the other two is removed, then the all-singleton product. This is the form that
says in its own syntax that third order is what survives second order.

definitions.name: Descent.PopGen.driftVariance
definitions.docstring:
**Drift variance for a single population.**
    `Var(p_t - p₀) = p₀(1-p₀) × F`, with `F` the PER-BRANCH drift coefficient --
    the fraction of ancestral heterozygosity this one lineage has lost since the
    split, Wright's `F` against the ancestor.

    Convention: `fst` is that per-branch `F`, not the pairwise Hudson `F_ST` of
    `PortabilityDrift.fstFromTau` and not Nei's `G_ST`. The section note above
    gives the three conversions and the size of each mistake; the short version
    is that Hudson agrees only to first order (`0.500` against `0.632` at
    `τ = 1`) and Nei's `G_ST` is exactly half of what this argument wants.

    Empirical status: **VALIDATED**, and the design is what earns that -- an earlier
    reading of this docstring headlined it VACUOUS, which was wrong and is corrected here.
    The vacuity is a property of a DESIGN, not of this definition. `battery_bulk21` scored a
    MATCH that carried no information, because it estimated `F_ST` on the same run as
    `Var(p) / (p₀(1-p₀))`, and substituting that relation into this body gives
    `p₀(1-p₀) · Var(p) / (p₀(1-p₀))`, which is `Var(p)` -- the estimator itself,
    residual exactly `0` under computer algebra, using no Wright-Fisher property
    beyond the martingale `E[p_t] = p₀`. That design could not have rejected any
    competitor, so it measured nothing.

    A design that takes `F` from the MODEL instead is not an identity, and it is
    the one that settles the convention question the paragraph above raises:
    **VALIDATED** (`simcov/battery_bulk41.py`, `group_b`). The design
    escapes the identity above by never feeding the sample's own heterozygosity loss back
    in. `F` is the MODEL's `1-(1-1/(2Nₑ))^t`, computed from the simulation's `Nₑ` and `t`
    alone; the observable is the realised `Var(p₁ - p₀)` over 2×10⁵ independent loci under
    Wright-Fisher binomial sampling in two demes from a common ancestor at `p₀ = 0.3`, with no
    mutation and no migration.

      Nₑ    t     F        this body   realised Var   sems
      200    50   0.1176    0.02470      0.02464      0.85
      200   150   0.3130    0.06574      0.06556      0.96
      500   100   0.0952    0.01999      0.01997      0.44
      100    40   0.1817    0.03815      0.03817      0.14

    The identity gate carries the two substitutions the paragraph above warns about, each
    MEASURED on the same replicates rather than converted. Nei's `G_ST` misses by up to 157
    sems, 47% low, which is the promised factor of two. The Hudson pairwise `F_ST` misses by
    7.8 sems, 2.3% -- the first-order agreement the note predicts, and small enough to
    explain why that substitution has gone unnoticed elsewhere in the corpus. The positive
    control, drift is unbiased so `E[p_t] = p₀`, passes at 0.95 sems.

    Power: the prediction spans 0.01999 to 0.06574 across the four cells, `F`
    running from 0.0952 to 0.3130, and both convention substitutions ride those
    same replicates rather than being converted -- Nei's `G_ST` missing by up to
    157 sems and 47 percent low, the Hudson pairwise `F_ST` by 7.8 sems and 2.3
    percent.

definitions.name: Descent.PopGen.twoPopDriftVariance
definitions.docstring:
**Two-population drift variance from independent lineages.**
    For two populations diverging independently from the same
    ancestor, Var(p₁ - p₂) = Var(p₁) + Var(p₂) = 2·driftVariance.
    The factor of 2 comes from independence of drift.

    Empirical status: **VALIDATED**. As at `driftVariance`, an earlier reading of this
    docstring headlined it VACUOUS; that was wrong, because vacuity here is a property of a
    DESIGN and not of this definition, and it is corrected. `battery_bulk21`'s MATCH
    did carry no information: substituting the simulator's own
    `F_ST := Var(p)/(p₀(1-p₀))` collapses this onto
    `2·Var(p)`, which is what the simulator computes for `Var(p₁ - p₂)` once the two
    lineages are drawn independently — residual exactly `0`. The factor of `2` the docstring
    argues for is therefore assumed by the estimator, not tested by it. UNTESTED as a claim
    about the world.

    THE FACTOR OF TWO IS NOW TESTED: **VALIDATED** (`simcov/battery_bulk41.py`, `group_b`),
    by the design described at `driftVariance` -- `F` from the model's `Nₑ` and `t`, never
    from the sample -- with the observable being the realised `E[(p₁ - p₂)²]` over 2×10⁵
    independent loci in two independently drifting demes.

      Nₑ    t     F        this body   realised E[(p₁-p₂)²]   sems
      200    50   0.1176    0.04941         0.04932           0.61
      200   150   0.3130    0.13147         0.13129           0.46
      500   100   0.0952    0.03999         0.03991           0.61
      100    40   0.1817    0.07631         0.07636           0.23

    Dropping the factor of two on the SAME cells misses by up to 168 sems, 50% low, so the
    two is now carried by data rather than by the estimator's definition. Feeding the
    measured Hudson `F_ST` instead misses by 7.6 sems, 2.3%.

    Power: the prediction spans 0.03999 to 0.13147 across the four cells, `F`
    running from 0.0952 to 0.3130, and dropping the factor of two on those same
    cells misses by up to 168 sems and 50 percent low.

definitions.name: Descent.PopGen.expectedFreqDiffSq
definitions.docstring:
**Expected allele frequency difference from drift.**
    `E[(p₁ - p₂)²] = 2 × F × p₀(1-p₀)`, `p₀` the ancestral frequency and `F` the
    per-branch drift coefficient of `driftVariance`.

    Convention: the `2` is the count of independently drifting branches, and it
    is the constant that goes wrong when the argument is read as a pairwise
    differentiation instead. Against Nei's `G_ST` the same expectation is
    `4·G_ST·p̄·(1-p̄)`, so `fst := neiGst p₁ p₂` halves this body. See the
    section note.

    Empirical status: **VALIDATED**. An earlier reading of this docstring headlined it
    VACUOUS; that was wrong for the reason given at `driftVariance` -- vacuity is a property
    of a design, not of a definition -- and it is corrected here.
    `battery_bulk21`'s MATCH carried no information; this body is `twoPopDriftVariance`
    with its arguments in the other order, so it collapses onto the simulator's `2·Var(p)`
    for the same reason and with the same exactly-`0` residual. Note what that means for the
    convention paragraph above: the factor-of-2 question and the Nei/Hudson question are
    precisely what the simulation could NOT answer, because the estimator it compared
    against carried the corpus's own convention in its definition of `fst`. UNTESTED as a
    claim about the world; the convention is open and a simulation pinned to the convention
    cannot close it.

    A SIMULATION NOT PINNED TO THE CONVENTION CLOSES IT: **VALIDATED**
    (`simcov/battery_bulk41.py`, `group_b`). The escape is to take `F` from the model --
    `1-(1-1/(2Nₑ))^t`, a function of the simulation's parameters and nothing else -- and to
    MEASURE the Hudson `F_ST` and Nei `G_ST` separately on the same replicates as
    competitors, so all three conventions are numbers the run produced rather than one
    convention evaluated twice.

      Nₑ    t     F        this body   realised E[(p₁-p₂)²]   sems
      200    50   0.1176    0.04941         0.04932           0.61
      200   150   0.3130    0.13147         0.13129           0.46
      500   100   0.0952    0.03999         0.03991           0.61
      100    40   0.1817    0.07631         0.07636           0.23

    Both questions the paragraph above called unanswerable are answered on these cells: the
    factor of two is confirmed, since halving misses by 168 sems, and the Nei reading is
    refuted at 157 sems and 47% low -- the promised halving. The Hudson reading misses by
    only 2.3%, which is the first-order agreement and the reason it is a trap rather than an
    obvious error.

    Power: the prediction spans 0.03999 to 0.13147 across the four cells, `F`
    running from 0.0952 to 0.3130, and all three conventions are numbers this run
    produced rather than one convention evaluated twice: halving misses by 168
    sems, the Nei reading is refuted at 157 sems and 47 percent low, and the
    Hudson reading is out by 2.3 percent.

definitions.name: Descent.PopGen.taggedEffect
definitions.docstring:
Apparent effect recovered through a tag at LD correlation `tagR` to the
causal variant.

    Regime: one causal variant, one tag, both standardized; the apparent effect
    is the tag's MARGINAL regression coefficient.

    Empirical status: **VALIDATED** (`simcov/battery_bulk22.py`, `group_b`).
    One causal variant and one tag at correlation `r`, both standardized, over
    2×10⁶ individuals; the observable is the tag's REALISED marginal OLS slope.
    `r` is swept from 0.3 to 0.9, over which `r` and `r²` separate threefold.

      β_c    r     this body   realised slope   sems
      0.3   0.9     0.270000      0.269586       0.61
      0.3   0.5     0.150000      0.150119       0.17
      0.5   0.7     0.350000      0.350293       0.44
      0.2   0.3     0.060000      0.060220       0.31

    The identity gate is carried: the squared form `β_c · r²` is run on the SAME
    cells and misses by 39 to 159 sems — at `r = 0.3` it predicts 0.018 against
    a measured 0.0602 — and the positive control, the causal variant's own
    slope, which must be `β_c`, passes at 0.02 sems. A match with no rejected
    competitor would have measured nothing.

    CORRECTED. This body previously took squared LD. Regressing the phenotype
    on the tag recovers
    `Cov(g_tag, y) = β_c · r`, and a standardized tag has unit variance, so no
    second factor of `r` divides it out. Both forms were carried on the same
    cells, so the exponent was chosen by the data and not by the parameter's
    name.

    `r²` remains the right argument for quantities QUADRATIC in the effect --
    the variance a tag explains is `β_c² · r²`, and there the square belongs.
    It is the linear effect that takes `r`. The sign matters too and `r²`
    discards it: two tags in equal-magnitude but opposite-sign LD carry
    apparent effects of opposite sign.

    WHAT THE LEDGER NOW SAYS, in its own voice. The verdict above is
    `bulk22` `group_b`, and this paragraph is about that row rather than a
    second reading of it -- one docstring states its status once, and the
    marker is the one at the top.

    THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO SAY THE LEDGER COULD NOT SAY THIS ABOUT ITSELF, and
    that was true of the ledger and not of the harness. `bulk22` recorded
    `causalEffect * tagR2` as the corpus row and `causalEffect * tagR` as the
    challenger; the corpus took the challenger and the labels stayed, so the
    ledger carried a falsification against this NAME whose `source` field was
    the superseded formula. A reader who greps for the name and not for the
    source reached the opposite conclusion. The roles in that battery are now
    the right way round, so the ledger states the verdict directly and this
    docstring no longer has to translate it.

    Power: the prediction spans 0.060000 to 0.350000 across the four cells, with
    `r` swept from 0.3 to 0.9 so that `r` and `r²` separate threefold, and the
    squared form `β_c · r²` runs on those same cells and misses by 39 to 159
    sems.

definitions.name: Descent.PopGen.gwasHeritability
definitions.docstring:
**LD tagging efficiency.**
    The proportion of heritability captured by GWAS depends on
    how well the genotyped SNPs tag causal variants:
    h²_GWAS = h²_true × average_r²_tag.

    Regime: `h²_true` is the heritability the effects actually carry, not a
    nominal per-effect variance times a locus count. The distinction is not
    pedantic and it is what a measurement of this definition turns on -- see
    below.

    Empirical status: **VALIDATED**
    (`validation/empirical/simcov/battery_dis1.py`). 100000 individuals,
    300 causal variants each tagged by one variant at correlation `rho`,
    heritability captured by regressing the outcome on the TAGS, with the
    in-sample `R²` corrected for its `m/n` optimism:

      design              this def   captured
      h² = 0.5, rho = 0.9  0.40590   0.40681 ± 0.00257   (0.35 sems)
      h² = 0.5, rho = 0.6  0.18777   0.18793 ± 0.00119   (0.14 sems)
      h² = 0.8, rho = 0.8  0.51355   0.50972 ± 0.00322   (1.19 sems)

    **A retraction** (`battery_bulk5.py`). That battery reported this definition
    FALSIFIED at 42 sems and 23 percent low. The report is withdrawn: it drew 60
    effects from `N(0, h²/M)` and then compared against the NOMINAL `h²`. The
    realised heritability of 60 such draws scatters by `sqrt(2/60)`, about 18
    percent, which is the whole of the reported error -- the same runs agree to
    0.35 sems once `h²_true` is read as the heritability the drawn effects
    actually produce. The definition never claimed to know what a finite draw
    would realise.

    Power: the prediction spans 0.18777 to 0.51355 across the design.

    **The exponent is chosen by the data** (`simcov/battery_bulk29.py`,
    `group_b`), which the run above did not establish. An independent design --
    200 causal variants each with one tag, the phenotype built from the CAUSAL
    variants and the score fitted on the TAGS, 300000 individuals -- reproduces
    this body at worst 3.51 sems (1.2% relative) with `r` swept 0.3 to 0.9.
    Carried on the same cells, the UNSQUARED form `h²_true · r` is FALSIFIED at
    up to 652 sems (225% relative). So the square is not a convention: a tag
    recovers heritability, which is quadratic in the effect, through `r²`, while
    it recovers the EFFECT itself through `r` -- see `taggedEffect`, where the
    corpus had the exponents the other way round.

definitions.name: Descent.PopGen.populationGeneVariance
definitions.docstring: Total gene-level variance is the sum of shared and population-specific components.

definitions.name: Descent.PopGen.crossPopulationGeneTransferFraction
definitions.docstring: Fraction of a target population's gene-level variance carried by shared variants.

Number of distinct causal signals across two populations after shared signals are
counted only once.

definitions.name: Descent.PopGen.geneFlowFstStep
definitions.docstring:
**One generation of gene flow against drift**, in the architecture file's
argument order.

This is `ibdFlowStep` with the homogenising force taken to be
migration: `F` is the probability that two gene copies from the same population
are identical by descent, drift adds `(1 - F)/(2 Nₑ)` and migration removes
`2 m F`.  It is written here, rather than only in `PortabilityDrift`, because
the obligation to derive `fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium` belongs to the file that states it;
`geneFlowFstStep_eq_ibdFlowStep` records that it is the same map.

Composition convention: drift and gene flow are added, not composed, which is
the weak-migration/large-`Nₑ` first-order model.  The unlinearised multiplicative
recursion `islandFstMultiplicativeStep` has a different fixed point.

    Empirical status: **VALIDATED**, including the argument
    forwarding (`validation/empirical/simcov/battery_bulk14.py`).
    Wright-Fisher forward simulation, 4000 loci, 300 replicate populations, one
    generation of drift plus gene flow from a fixed source pool, `F` read as
    `1 - H/H_ancestral`:

      Ne     rate     this def   simulated            sems
      200    0.002     0.07045   0.07050 ± 0.00028     0.15
      500    0.005     0.02602   0.02599 ± 0.00010     0.23
      200    0.010     0.05502   0.05497 ± 0.00022     0.22

    The forwarding is the point of the test. This definition's signature is
    `(m Ne F)` while the `ibdFlowStep` it delegates to is `(Ne rate F)`, so the
    first two arguments are exchanged in the call and a wrapper that failed to
    exchange them would be indistinguishable by eye. The battery calls this
    definition at its OWN order with the rate and `Ne` five orders apart: a
    transposed forwarding would return 205.61, 72.20 and 25.88 against a
    measurement near 0.05. The forwarding is correct, and it is now correct for
    a reason that a reader can check against numbers.

    Power: the prediction spans 0.026 to 0.070 across the design.

definitions.name: Descent.PopGen.AssortativeMatingModel.witness
definitions.body:
1 / 2
  V_A := 1
  V_P := 2
  r_pos := by norm_num
  r_lt_one := by norm_num
  V_A_pos := by norm_num

definitions.docstring:
**The class is inhabited.**  A theorem quantified over an uninhabited structure is
true and empty: kernel-checked, clean axiom report, no content.  This is the witness that
makes the theorems below statements about something.

definitions.name: Descent.PopGen.AssortativeMatingModel.h2
definitions.docstring:
**Narrow-sense heritability**, the ratio of additive to total variance.

**Computed, not a field pinned by a hypothesis.** A parameter fixed by an equation is
not a parameter: it can be supplied inconsistently only by supplying a false proof, and
every model then carries the equation around. Because this is computed, `h2_def` is `rfl`
and positivity and the upper bound are theorems rather than assumptions.

hypotheses: 0 ≤ Real.sqrt R2₁ * Real.sqrt m.h_sq * m.case_mean - T'
0 ≤ T' - Real.sqrt R2₁ * Real.sqrt m.h_sq * μ_control
ThresholdRegime m T' μ_control r2_target r2_source
ThresholdRegime m T' μ_control r2_unvalidated r2_validated

Descent.Portability.liabilitySpecificity: 0 ≤ T' - Real.sqrt R2₁ * Real.sqrt m.h_sq * μ_control
